gm.title: Description
lines: A winter hag who rides a flying staff and uses blizzards to turn isolated settlements against one another.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Graystaff Magic. The hag can ride her graystaff as a Broom of Flying. Holding it lets her cast the staff spells under Innate Spellcasting. Only a bheur hag can use the staff. Replacing it after loss or destruction takes a year and a day.
Ice Walk. The hag can walk and climb on ice without ability checks. Ice and snow that count as difficult terrain cost her no additional movement.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d8 + 1) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.
Maddening Feast. The hag feeds on the corpse of an enemy within 5 ft. that died in the past minute. Any creatures she chooses within 60 ft. that can see her must make a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, a creature is frightened of her for 1 minute. While frightened this way, it is incapacitated. It cannot read or understand speech and speaks only gibberish. The DM controls its erratic movement. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A successful save or the end of the effect makes the creature immune to this hag's Maddening Feast for 24 hours.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines:
The hag uses Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks) and needs no material components.
At will. Ray of Frost.
1/day. Control Weather.
While holding the graystaff. Hold Person at will. Cone of Cold, Ice Storm, and Wall of Ice 3/day each.

gm.title: Coven challenge
lines: A bheur hag in a coven is CR 9 (5,000 XP). Use the Bheur Hag (Coven) profile for standard shared spells, or the Death, Nature, or Prophecy profile for the corresponding spell list.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
Optional lair actions for powerful hags. Grandmothers usually have three to five options. Aunties usually have at most one. On initiative count 20, after any creature tied with the hag, she can use one available option while in her lair and able to act. She cannot use the same option in consecutive rounds. If surprised, she must finish her first turn before she can use one. If an effect calls for a saving throw without giving a DC, use the DC of the hag's most powerful ability.
Pass Through Surfaces. The hag can pass through solid doors, walls, ceilings, and floors until initiative count 20 of the next round.
Doors and Windows. Open or close any number of visible doors and windows, choosing separately for each. A door closed this way can be magically locked. Forcing it open requires a DC 20 Strength check. The lock lasts until she unlocks the door or opens it with this lair action.
Blizzard. Center a cylinder 40 ft. tall and 20 ft. in radius on a point the hag can see within 120 ft. It lasts until initiative count 20 of the next round and lightly obscures creatures and objects in it. A creature that starts its turn there or enters for the first time on a turn is blinded until that same initiative count.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Pick regional effects for the hag's lair. A typical hag lair has three to five. Powerful hags and covens usually have more than a lone hag. If an effect calls for a save without giving a DC, use that of the hag's most powerful ability. When the hag dies or abandons the lair, effects can end immediately or fade within 2d10 days.
A grandmother's lair can produce any of the following within 1 mile. Appropriate small animals become unusually abundant. Beasts with Intelligence 2 or lower are charmed by the hag and act aggressively toward intruders at her direction. Carved figures, twig fetishes, or rag dolls appear in trees.
A powerful bheur hag can add any of the following within 1 mile. Snow slides can block routes or bury creatures, leaving them restrained and holding their breath until dug out. Human-sized blocks of ice contain bodies that can break out as zombies or release specters. Blizzards strike once every 2d12 hours and last 1d3 hours, halving overland speed and reducing normal visibility to 30 ft. Routes can loop back on themselves, making navigation difficult.

lines:

Level 1 (4 shared slots). Identify, Ray Of Sickness.
Level 2 (3 shared slots). Hold Person, Locate Object.
Level 3 (3 shared slots). Bestow Curse, Counterspell, Lightning Bolt.
Level 4 (3 shared slots). Phantasmal Killer, Polymorph.
Level 5 (2 shared slots). Contact Other Plane, Scrying.
Level 6 (1 shared slot). Eyebite.

gm.title: Hag Eye mechanics
lines: A coven can keep one Hag Eye at a time. It has AC 10, 1 hit point, and darkvision 60 ft. Any member on the same plane as the eye can use an action to see through it. If the eye is destroyed, each member takes 3d10 psychic damage and is blinded for 24 hours. Making one takes an hour with all three hags present. None can be blinded. If any takes another action during the ritual, they must start over.

A grandmother's lair can produce any of the following within 1 mile. Appropriate small animals become unusually abundant. Beasts with Intelligence 2 or lower are charmed by the hag and act aggressively toward intruders at her direction. Carved figures, twig fetishes, or rag dolls appear in trees.
A powerful bheur hag can add any of the following within 1 mile. Snow slides can block routes or bury creatures, leaving them restrained and holding their breath until dug out. Human-sized blocks of ice contain bodies that can break out as zombies or release specters. Blizzards strike once every 2d12 hours and last 1d3 hours, halving overland speed and reducing normal visibility to 30 ft. Routes can loop back on themselves, making navigation difficult.

gm.title: Shared coven spellcasting
lines:
All three members must be within 30 ft. of one another to cast these spells. They draw from a single pool of slots, so one hag's casting spends a slot for the whole coven. Each counts as a 12th-level spellcaster for these wizard spells and uses Intelligence (save DC 13, +5 to hit).
Level 1 (4 shared slots). Bane, Bless.
Level 2 (3 shared slots). Augury, Detect Thoughts.
Level 3 (3 shared slots). Clairvoyance, Dispel Magic, Nondetection.
Level 4 (3 shared slots). Arcane Eye, Locate Creature.
Level 5 (2 shared slots). Geas, Legend Lore.
Level 6 (1 shared slot). True Seeing.

gm.title: Hag Eye mechanics
lines: A coven can keep one Hag Eye at a time. It has AC 10, 1 hit point, and darkvision 60 ft. Any member on the same plane as the eye can use an action to see through it. If the eye is destroyed, each member takes 3d10 psychic damage and is blinded for 24 hours. Making one takes an hour with all three hags present. None can be blinded. If any takes another action during the ritual, they must start over.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
False Appearance (object form). A motionless mimic passes for an ordinary object.
Mimicry. The mimic can imitate sounds it has heard, including voices. A listener can recognize the imitation with a DC 12 Wisdom (Insight) check.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) acid damage. A Large or smaller creature hit this way is Grappled (escape DC 15).
Gnashing Maw. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing plus 10 (3d6) acid damage. If the mimic is grappling the target, deal an extra 3 (1d6) acid damage.
Shapechanger. The mimic can become any object of Medium size or larger or return to its true amorphous form. Its size is the only statistic that changes. Worn or carried gear keeps its shape. On death the mimic resumes its true form.
Envelop. While grappling a creature, the mimic uses Shapechanger to become an object at least as large as that creature if it is not already in such a form. The creature is then enveloped and its grapple ends. It cannot breathe, is Blinded and Restrained, and has total cover from attacks and effects outside the mimic. It moves with the mimic and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the mimic’s turns.
The mimic can envelop one creature at a time. An engulfed creature can spend an action to make a DC 15 Strength check, escaping into an empty space of its choice within 5 ft. of the mimic on a success. It also escapes automatically if the mimic uses Shapechanger or Panic Shift, becomes Incapacitated, or dies.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Panic Shift (1/day). When it takes damage, the mimic releases any Grappled or enveloped creatures and becomes a Small, dense, spiked object. In this form its walking and climbing speeds double, it resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from mundane attacks, and its actions are limited to Dash, Disengage, and Shapechanger. A creature within 5 ft. that touches it or hits it with a melee attack takes 10 (3d6) piercing damage. This ends when the mimic dies or uses Shapechanger to take another form.

lines: The variant keeps the base block’s true-form size and printed physical damage. Its listed changes add acid damage to both attacks and allow it to assume larger object forms.

lines: A black dragon can reach this form by drawing together the power of its counterparts across worlds. Acid runs through its breath and its mythic flare.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Chromatic Awakening (recharges after a short or long rest). When the creature would drop to 0 HP, set its current HP to 425, recharge Breath Weapon, and restore all spent uses of Legendary Resistance. The creature can take mythic actions for the following hour. Award 105,000 extra XP if defeated after this trait activates (210,000 XP total).
Legendary Resistance (4/day). Turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 20) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can hold only one creature with this attack at a time.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Breath Weapon (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 26 Dexterity save, taking 78 (12d12) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The creature has 3 legendary actions. It can take one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains spent actions at the start of its turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its flying speed.
Arcane Spear (3 actions). Create four spears of magical force. Each spear hits a creature the greatwyrm chooses and can see within 120 ft., dealing 12 (1d8 + 8) force damage before disappearing.

gm.title: Mythic actions
lines:
For 1 hour after Chromatic Awakening activates, the greatwyrm can spend legendary actions on these options.
Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Chromatic Flare (2 actions). Each creature in a 60-ft.-radius sphere centered on the greatwyrm must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 22 (5d8) acid damage.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: An Izzet mixture of water and molten rock. Magical fire feeds its growth until the accumulated energy bursts free.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold and fire. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Elemental Nature. The weird needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Feed on Fire. Fire damage from a spell or another magical effect increases the weird’s size by one category, limited by available space. At Large or bigger, it has advantage on Strength checks and saves. If it starts its turn Gargantuan, it explodes and returns to Medium. Each creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 12 Dexterity save, taking 28 (8d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. The explosion ignites flammable objects that nobody wears or carries.
Form of Fire and Water. The weird can pass through gaps as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing. It can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. The first time the weird enters any given creature’s space on a turn, the creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage and ignites. It takes another 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until someone uses an action to douse the fire.
Heated Body. A creature that touches the weird or hits it in melee from within 5 ft. takes 5 (1d10) fire damage.
Illumination. It sheds bright light for 30 ft. and dim light for another 30 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Slam. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning plus 7 (2d6) fire damage. If the weird is Large or bigger, use 11 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning plus 14 (4d6) fire damage instead.

gm.title: Base stat block
lines: Delerium Dreg, Appendix A, p. 199. This profile includes the printed Bloated mutation.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Misty Camouflage. The dreg has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in mist or fog that obscures the area.
Death Burst. When the dreg dies, each creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 11 Constitution save. A creature takes 7 (2d6) necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. A failure by at least 5 also adds one level of contamination.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, 5-ft. reach or 20/60-ft. range, one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage. Wielding the spear in two hands for a melee attack deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
Bile Spray (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 11 Dexterity save. A creature takes 7 (2d6) acid damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. A failure by at least 5 also adds one level of contamination.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Haze-native creatures
lines:
Printed source. Appendix A, pp. 196–197. These traits leave the creature’s CR as printed. They apply to Haze natives and exclude creatures recruited or summoned by the party.
Fully Contaminated. Immune to contamination and has advantage on saves against contaminated spells.
Haze Adaptation. Can benefit from a long rest in the Haze. It can see twice as far through the Haze and Deep Haze.
Haze Dependence. Gains one Exhaustion level for each 24 hours outside the Haze. It can remove those levels only in the Haze.
Delerium Healing. As an action, touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) HP. That shard cannot heal this way again for 24 hours.

gm.title: Description
lines: A colossal ooze that engulfs prey and debris alike. Destroying its body sends whatever it has engulfed into the Astral Sea.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Stunned, Unconscious.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Astral Implosion. At 0 HP, the blob implodes, sending engulfed creatures and objects to the Astral Sea. It vanishes and coats everything that was within 600 ft. with slime. It reforms on a random world on the Material Plane in 1d20 years.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). On a failed saving throw, the blob can spend one use to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The blob has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Pseudopod attacks and use Engulf. One Pseudopod attack can be replaced with Restraining Glob.
Pseudopod. Melee attack, +15 to hit, reach 30 ft. A hit deals 24 (3d10 + 8) Force damage.
Engulf. Move up to the blob's Speed, passing through spaces occupied by Huge or smaller creatures or objects. Each target makes a DC 23 Strength save the first time the blob enters its space during this move. Failure engulfs the target. Engulfed targets move with the blob and have Total Cover against attacks and effects outside it. A nonmagical object is destroyed after 1 minute inside. An engulfed creature is Restrained and suffocating, takes 21 (6d6) Force damage at the start of each of its turns, and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. If it drops to 0 HP while engulfed, it dissolves into ash and the blob ejects the ash into the Astral Sea. On a successful save, the target escapes to the nearest unoccupied space.
Restraining Glob. Choose one visible Large or smaller creature within 600 ft. It makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 18 (3d6 + 8) Acid damage, rolls 60 ft. straight toward the blob, and is Restrained until the end of its next turn, when the glob dissolves harmlessly. Success halves the damage and avoids the movement and restraint.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses. Spend one immediately after another creature's turn to select one option. The blob recovers spent uses at the start of its turn and cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Decay. Each creature engulfed by the blob takes 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage. The blob cannot use this option again until the start of its next turn.
Grasping Glob. Use Restraining Glob. The blob cannot use this option again until the start of its next turn.
Lashing Goop. Make one Pseudopod attack.

gm.title: Description
lines: An undead predator that can turn a victim’s blood into an infatuating bond. Blood drinkers haunt Ravnica’s alleys and sewers, and some collect blood tithes for the Orzhov Syndicate.

On a hit, deal 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. A humanoid hit makes a DC 15 Charisma save. On a failure, the vampire charms it for 1 minute and it becomes infatuated with the vampire for that duration. Reduce the target’s hit point maximum by the necrotic damage it took. The vampire regains the same amount. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if its hit point maximum reaches 0.

Attack Slam +6 melee (1d8 + 4 plus Blood Drain). Full attack Slam +6 melee (1d8 + 4 plus Blood Drain).

Feats include Power Attack. Advancement 5–7 HD, Medium.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Slam. Make one melee slam, or use the full-attack count in the chosen tier. Blood Drain applies to every successful slam against a living creature.
Blood Drain (Ex). After a slam hits a living creature, the elemental attempts to drain its blood as a free action. Fortitude DC equals its HD plus its Constitution modifier. Failure deals 1d4 Constitution damage. The elemental gains 1 HP for each point of Constitution damage actually dealt.
Drench (Ex). Touch extinguishes an exposed nonmagical flame at least one size category smaller than the elemental. Touching magical fire can dispel it as dispel magic at caster level equal to the elemental’s HD.
Engulf (Ex). The elemental can engulf a foe at least one size smaller in a round when it makes no slams. The target can make an attack of opportunity and forgo the save, or decline the attack and attempt a DC 16 Reflex save. An engulfed creature is subject to the 3.5 drowning rules. When an attack hits the elemental, split the damage evenly between it and the engulfed target on a 50% roll if the elemental is one size larger, or 10% if it is two sizes larger. With a gap of three or more categories, only the elemental takes damage.

Exceptionally evil blood can increase its HD. It cannot enter or cross a large body of water. Forced contact with a body of water at least as large as itself deals 1d10 damage each round until it escapes.

gm.title: Drowning
lines: In 3.5, a creature can hold its breath for twice its Constitution score in rounds. Each standard or full-round action uses an additional round of that reserve. Once it runs out, make a DC 10 Constitution check each round, increasing the DC by 1 each round. On a failure it falls unconscious at 0 HP, drops to −1 HP in the following round, and dies in the third.

gm.title: Dread elemental rules
lines:
Printed source. Elemental, Dread, p. 63, and Mists subtype, pp. 7–8.
In Ravenloft, calling a standard elemental has a 20% chance of producing a dread elemental. Summoning magic always produces the dread form. Accidental dread elementals are uncontrolled, and the Dark Powers supply the matching materials. Intentional conjuring requires the matching material and uses the usual chance for the elemental to break control.
Dread elementals understand speech but do not communicate. Their Mists subtype makes them native throughout Ravenloft and allows them to be summoned in any domain. A dismissed dread elemental returns to Ravenloft itself, so the realm's restrictions on calling do not break the calling pact.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Blood Drain uses HD plus Constitution modifier as printed. The DCs in printed tier order are 3, 7, 12, 21, 26, and 29.
The Large block gives a space of 5 ft. and DR 10/—. Its Huge tier has DR 5/—. These are the printed values.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A horned hobgoblin warlord in dark plate, brandishing a curved sword and purple flaming skulls.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Plate armor. Saves Wis +5, Cha +5. Arcana +3, Athletics +7, History +3, Intimidation +5. Resists fire and necrotic damage. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12. Common, Goblin, Infernal.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Infernal Ichor. When Varrox dies, each creature within 5 ft. takes 5 fire damage.
Infernal Sacrifice (3/day). When Varrox fails a saving throw, he can turn it into a success. Each ally within 60 ft. then takes 5 necrotic damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Soulsword and Death Skulls.
Soulsword. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. A creature hit cannot regain HP until the start of Varrox’s next turn.
Death Skulls. Ranged weapon attack +7, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing plus 9 (2d8) fire damage. On a hit, Varrox can teleport to a vacant space he can see within 5 ft. of the target.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Advance and Attack. Choose one ally within 60 ft. who can hear Varrox. That ally can spend its reaction to move up to its speed and make a weapon attack.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: An Army from Blood. When a non-minion hobgoblin Varrox can see within 60 ft. takes damage, Varrox magically summons three hobgoblin recruits in the vacant spaces nearest that hobgoblin.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Use each once per encounter, in any order after an enemy’s turn. Use at most one per round.
Uncanny Leadership. Choose up to six non-minion allies within 60 ft. who can see or hear Varrox. Varrox and each chosen ally gain 10 temporary HP and can move up to their speed.
Hellish Transport. Varrox and each ally within 60 ft. can teleport up to 60 ft. to a vacant space that creature can see.
I Am Fire and Death. Enemies within 20 ft. make a DC 15 Constitution save against 11 (2d10) fire plus 11 (2d10) necrotic damage, taking half as much on success. Black flames then surround Varrox for 1 minute. Each time a creature touches him or hits him with an attack from within 5 ft., it takes 5 (1d10) fire plus 5 (1d10) necrotic damage.

gm.title: Encounter uses

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A horned hobgoblin warlord in dark plate, brandishing a curved sword and purple flaming skulls.

lines: Plate armor. Saves Wis +5, Cha +5. Arcana +3, Athletics +7, History +3, Intimidation +5. Resists fire and necrotic damage. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12. Common, Goblin, Infernal.

lines:

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Soulsword and Death Skulls.
Soulsword. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. A creature hit cannot regain HP until the start of Varrox’s next turn.
Death Skulls. Ranged weapon attack +7, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing plus 9 (2d8) fire damage. On a hit, Varrox can teleport to a vacant space he can see within 5 ft. of the target.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Advance and Attack. Choose one ally within 60 ft. who can hear Varrox. That ally can spend its reaction to move up to its speed and make a weapon attack.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: An Army from Blood. When a non-minion hobgoblin Varrox can see within 60 ft. takes damage, Varrox magically summons three hobgoblin recruits in the vacant spaces nearest that hobgoblin.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Use each once per encounter, in any order after an enemy’s turn. Use at most one per round.
Uncanny Leadership. Choose up to six non-minion allies within 60 ft. who can see or hear Varrox. Varrox and each chosen ally gain 10 temporary HP and can move up to their speed.
Hellish Transport. Varrox and each ally within 60 ft. can teleport up to 60 ft. to a vacant space that creature can see.
I Am Fire and Death. Enemies within 20 ft. make a DC 15 Constitution save against 11 (2d10) fire plus 11 (2d10) necrotic damage, taking half as much on success. Black flames then surround Varrox for 1 minute. Each time a creature touches him or hits him with an attack from within 5 ft., it takes 5 (1d10) fire plus 5 (1d10) necrotic damage.

gm.title: Encounter uses
lines: Varrox trains his army in Camp Firefield, a demiplane reached through his pavilion. His line officers give him targets for Advance and Attack and can trigger his recruit summons when wounded.

gm.title: Description
lines: Blue slaadi fight beside red slaadi. Their claw blades carry a curse called chaos phage, and they instinctively avoid killing creatures already bearing a slaad curse.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Magic Resistance. The creature makes saving throws with Advantage against spells and other magical effects.
Regeneration. The slaad regains 10 HP at the start of each of its turns while it has at least 1 HP.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Mutating Claw attacks.
Mutating Claw. Melee attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage. A Humanoid hit by the claw makes a DC 15 Constitution save if it carries no slaad curse. On a failure it contracts chaos phage. While cursed, it can't regain HP and loses 10 (3d6) from its HP maximum every 24 hours. A Long Rest doesn't restore the lost maximum.
If the curse reduces the target's HP maximum to 0, the curse ends and the target immediately becomes a Red Slaad. It becomes a Green Slaad instead if it can cast spells of level 3 or higher. The transformation replaces death. Only Wish can undo the transformation.

gm.title: Slaad control gems
lines:
A slaad born from the Spawning Stone carries a magical control gem in its head. Once another creature claims the gem, the slaad is Charmed and obeys the bearer. It stops being Charmed if the bearer or the bearer's allies harm it, if someone returns the gem to the slaad, or if Greater Restoration destroys the gem when cast on the slaad.
Wish can retrieve the gem. If the slaad fails its save against Imprisonment, the caster gets the gem and the slaad stays free. Removing the gem from an Incapacitated slaad takes 1 minute and a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Medicine) check. Failure deals 22 (4d10) Piercing damage to the slaad.

lines: Monster Manual (2024), p. 285. The Slaad Control Gems sidebar supplies the control gem rules.

gm.title: Slaad Control Gem
lines: A slaad created by a Spawning Stone has a control gem. A slaad that was born another way develops one on contact with the stone. Whoever holds the extracted gem can command the slaad, which is immune to being Charmed while under that control.

Wish can recover a gem, Imprisonment can transfer it on a failed save, and Greater Restoration destroys it harmlessly. A trained healer can spend 1 minute attempting extraction from an Incapacitated slaad with a DC 20 Wisdom (Medicine) check. On failure the slaad takes 4d10 psychic damage.

lines: Boggle Oil. Choose slippery or sticky coating. Slippery oil grants advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to get out of restraints, fit through a tight space, or break a grapple. lines:

Full Attack. Two slaps +2 melee (1d4 + 2 each). If both hit, the target is automatically grappled. Starting the next round, Constrict deals 2d4 + 2 each round. gm.title: Traits
lines:
Undead traits and damage reduction 5, bypassed by slashing or piercing weapons. The sample lists vulnerability to turning without giving a modifier. Holy water or the touch of a holy symbol deals 1d8 damage.
Pliability (Ex). It can squeeze through a gap at least 1 inch wide or fold into a 1-cubic-foot container, including an airtight one. Soak it at least once per week or keep it in a reservoir of water. If it dries out it loses its special maneuvers, including its grapple attack, and moves and fights as a zombie. A dried boneless takes double damage from fire.

gm.title: Creating a Boneless
lines:
Acquired template for a corporeal, formerly skeletal creature other than an undead, with fewer than 20 HD. Keep size. Replace type with undead and drop alignment and kind subtypes without adding the augmented subtype. Keep base statistics where the template gives no change. Drop class Hit Dice, to a minimum of 3 HD, and use d12s for current and future Hit Dice. Set speed to 30 ft. or 60 ft. on all fours. It cannot fly, even with wings.
Keep weapons and weapon proficiencies. Retain natural attacks except claws and bites. Each hand deals 1d4 + Strength bonus, and constriction after a successful grapple deals 2d4 + Strength bonus per round. Replace other special attacks with Constrict. Keep only extraordinary special qualities that enhance melee attacks and add the traits listed above.
Base saves are Fort and Ref +1 per 3 HD and Will +2 plus half HD. Dexterity increases by 2, Wisdom becomes 10, and Charisma becomes 1. Remove Constitution and Intelligence scores, skills, and prior feats. Gain Agility. CR starts at 3 and rises with HD. Advancement follows the base creature unless it advanced by class, in which case use none. Any environment or organization, no treasure or level adjustment, always evil and usually neutral evil.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The sample stat block and template use 2d4 + Strength for constriction. The general combat paragraph says 2d4. This summary uses the sample's explicit 2d4 + 2.
The sample lists Will +2. Its template's formula gives +3 at 3 HD. Use the listed sample save for this encounter and the template formula when creating another boneless.

gm.title: Description
lines: A drowned sailor rises to punish the crew it blames for its death. Its first appearance always falls on the anniversary of the accident.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC 13 (+2 Dex, +1 deflection), touch 13, flat-footed 11. Base attack +2, grapple +4. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +4, Ref +3, Will +2. Balance +6, Hide +8, Listen +8, Profession (sailor) +6, Search +8, Spot +10. Alertness (bonus), Dodge, Power Attack. Any aquatic environment. Solitary. No treasure. Always chaotic evil. Advancement 5–8 HD (Medium).

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +7 melee (1d6, or 1d6+7 against ethereal targets) or ghostly scimitar +7 melee (1d6+3).
Seasick Touch (Su). A hit on a living victim deals 1d6 damage. On a failed DC 15 Fortitude save, it also nauseates the victim until a Heal check or healing magic cures the nausea.
Manifestation (Su). While manifested, creatures on the Material or Ethereal Plane can attack the bowlyn, and it can strike with its touch or scimitar. Seeing it manifest causes fear as cast by a 12th-level sorcerer. DC 15 Will negates.
Telekinesis (Su). Once per round as a free action, as a 12th-level sorcerer. It can only move objects.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Incorporeal subtype, undead traits, and +5 turn resistance.

gm.title: Haunting
lines: It waits 1–10 years after death before returning. Once per night it engineers an accident against a former crewmate or where it worked on the ship. It uses Seasick Touch if it cannot cause an accident. It keeps returning until the crew dies or the ship is destroyed. Running the ship aground immediately destroys the spirit.

gm.title: Description
lines: The oldest brass dragons can fuse with counterparts from other worlds to become greatwyrms. A brass greatwyrm can breathe fire or sap its foes with gas.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Metallic Awakening (recharges after a short or long rest). When the creature would drop to 0 HP, set its current HP to 450, recharge Breath Weapon, and restore all spent uses of Legendary Resistance. The creature can take mythic actions for the following hour. Award 120,000 extra XP if defeated after this trait activates (240,000 XP total).
Legendary Resistance (4/day). Turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 20) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can hold only one creature with this attack at a time.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Breath Weapon (recharge 5–6). Choose Elemental Breath or Sapping Breath.
Elemental Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 84 (13d12) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sapping Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Constitution save. A failure leaves the creature unconscious for 1 minute. An unconscious creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds on the first save has disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of the greatwyrm’s next turn.
Change Shape. Magically take the form of any Medium or Small creature, retaining the greatwyrm’s statistics except size. The form ends if the greatwyrm drops to 0 HP or spends an action to end it.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The creature has 3 legendary actions. It can take one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains spent actions at the start of its turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its flying speed.

gm.title: Mythic actions
lines:
For 1 hour after Metallic Awakening activates, the greatwyrm can spend legendary actions on these options.
Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Shattering Roar (2 actions). Each creature in a 120-ft.-radius sphere centered on the greatwyrm must succeed on a DC 26 Constitution save or take 19 (3d12) thunder damage and be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Dragon customization
lines: Customize the dragon’s languages or skills to suit its history. Skill changes can include double proficiency or tool proficiencies. Other options on p. 34 include alternate senses and the Change Shape, Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation, and Tunneler traits or actions.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

Rejuvenation. After death, return at full HP in 1d6 months. A destroyed body reforms in the nearest unoccupied space to the place of death. The Wish spell or destruction of the giant’s true head stops this return.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

The target makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, its head lands at its feet. It survives while above 0 HP and is Blinded, Deafened, and unable to speak. A creature can spend an action to reattach the head and end the effect. Separation beyond 24 hours kills the target.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Get a Head. Attach a Giant or Humanoid head within 15 ft. to assume that creature’s form and size. The Bredbeddle can speak and see normally, gains the head’s special senses, and loses Headless. A creature within reach can spend an action and succeed on a DC 18 Strength (Athletics) check to remove it.

lines: Start with the giant in disguise on a road. Track the borrowed head separately from the giant’s true head and from any head removed during combat.

gm.title: Description
lines: A mouse-sized Feywild miner with its soul floating outside its body as a little light. Brigganocks pull wish stones from the earth and use bursts of accelerated time to finish jobs.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fey Ancestry. The brigganock has advantage on saves against being charmed, and magic cannot put it to sleep.
Soul Light. A tangible body does not contain this brigganock’s soul. It travels alongside the creature as an invulnerable, insubstantial light. It sheds bright light out to 10 ft. and dim light for another 10 ft. The brigganock cannot switch it off or adjust it. It fades when the brigganock dies.
Tunneler. With a pickaxe or similar tool, the brigganock can burrow through solid rock at 5 ft., leaving a 6-inch-wide tunnel.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

At will. Minor Illusion, Spare the Dying.
1/day each. Animal Friendship, Faerie Fire, Meld into Stone, Silence.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Move Soul Light. Move the light up to 30 ft. in any direction to an unoccupied space the brigganock can see. It returns at the end of the current turn.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: A mortal’s nonmagical wish can leave an echo inside a stone deep in the Feywild. Brigganocks keep and cut stones with kindly wishes and discard malicious ones. Powerful fey can use a wish stone to scry on the person who wished, power a supernatural charm, or awaken an animated object.

gm.title: Description
lines: A decrepit minotaur with a dented crown and a clay amphora wanders the Katachthon foothills. He claims Mogis cursed him after he chose his child as his heir, and now tests strangers for the right to succeed him.

gm.title: Starting hit points
lines: Antigonos uses the 2014 Minotaur and begins the encounter with 38 of its usual 76 HP. The listed Hit Dice and most other statistics come from the base creature.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Charge. After moving at least 10 ft. straight toward a target, hitting it with Gore on the same turn deals an extra 9 (2d8) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or be pushed up to 10 ft. away and knocked prone.
Labyrinthine Recall. Antigonos remembers every route he has traveled.
Reckless. At the start of his turn he can choose to gain advantage on melee weapon attack rolls that turn. If he does, attacks against him have advantage until the start of his next turn.
Decrepit State. Antigonos has disadvantage on his attack rolls.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d12 + 4) slashing damage.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Amphora. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If the amphora is empty, the target is restrained inside. A restrained creature can use an action to make a DC 14 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, escaping on a success. Destroying the amphora also ends the restraint. The amphora has AC 8, 20 HP, and immunity to poison and psychic damage.

gm.title: Test of the Amphora
lines:
Antigonos invites a Medium creature to climb into the amphora while he steadies it. After the creature enters, roll a d20.
1–9. He judges the creature too small and pours dirt into the amphora. The creature makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, it is blinded and restrained and begins suffocating. On a success, apply the effects of a hit from his Amphora attack.
10–19. He judges the creature too large and attacks it with his greataxe.
20. He declares the creature his heir, gives it his crown, robes, and belt pouch, and leaves.

gm.title: Contending with Antigonos
lines: He leaves if no one agrees to his test. Insults and theft can provoke him, and in a fight he may switch to random targets with his greataxe or empty amphora. If the party refrains from attacking him, he calms after a few rounds. A character who urges him to turn away from Mogis can make a DC 14 Charisma (Persuasion) check. On a success, he abandons the amphora and leaves to learn about a new deity. On a failure, he still departs in thought. Award experience for overcoming him whether or not the party fights.

gm.title: Printed source

Damage Reduction (Su). DR 10/magic.
Extra Limb (Ex). Add one slam to the full attack and gain Multiattack.
Frenzy (Ex), 1/day. Gain a +2 enhancement bonus to Strength and Constitution and take −2 AC until the broken one or its opponent dies.
Fluid Body (Su). Flatten and pass through any opening that water could pass through.
Improved Grab (Ex). A successful slam allows a free grapple attempt without provoking an attack of opportunity.
Inhuman Strength (Ex). Add 4 to Strength and raise melee attack and damage by 2.

gm.title: Tactics and languages
lines: It tends to charge without concern for its own safety. It understands the languages it knew before transformation but speaks them with difficulty. A specimen made from an animal often speaks its creator’s language.

Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.

gm.title: Description
lines: A ten-foot, one-eyed hunter with a gold-brown to umber hide. It needs days to digest a meal and fights only in self-defense while it digests.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Unusual Nature. The scavver needs no air.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Swallowing Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. The bite deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit by it must pass a DC 13 Dexterity save or be swallowed. The scavver can hold one creature at a time.
A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained. It has total cover from attacks and other effects outside the scavver. At the start of each of the scavver’s turns, gas in its gullet deals 13 (3d8) poison damage to the creature.
If a creature inside the scavver deals it at least 15 damage on a single turn, the scavver makes a DC 20 Constitution save at that turn’s end. On a failure, it regurgitates the creature, which lands prone within 10 ft. If the scavver dies, the swallowed creature is freed from restraint and can spend 10 ft. of movement to exit prone.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

lines:

lines:

lines: A corpse-dwelling scavenger whose eight legs resemble exposed ribs. It uses the corpse for cover and to anchor its tendrils.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC 17 (+2 size, +3 Dex, +2 natural), touch 15, flat-footed 14. Base attack +0, grapple −12. Space 2 ft., reach 15 ft. Fort +4, Ref +3, Will +0. Hide +18, Spot +4. Underground. gm.title: Actions
lines:
Tendrils (Ex). Tendril +5 ranged (1d2 plus pinning). Full attack, up to eight tendrils +5 ranged each (1d2 plus pinning per hit). On any hit, the target makes one Reflex save at DC 13 + the number of tendrils that hit or is pinned. The stalker itself is not considered grappled. Escape requires an Escape Artist or Strength check at DC 15 + the number of wrapping tendrils. Each tendril deals 1 damage per round to the bound target. An ally who uses Aid Another to help takes 1 damage. The stalker keeps attacking that target with tendrils that previously missed, at the printed +4 to hit. Each tendril has AC 20 (+8 size, +2 natural), 2 separate HP, and takes damage only from slashing weapons. Tendrils continue stinging for 1d4 rounds after the stalker dies.
Infest (Ex). Drag the pinned victim 5 ft. closer each round without provoking attacks of opportunity. When the victim reaches the stalker's square, release 2d4 larvae as a free action and die. If killed first, the stalker releases its larvae toward an adjacent creature. Larvae burrow on the following round. Before then, a helper who succeeds on a DC 15 Spot check can remove 1d4 larvae as a standard action. While larvae are burrowed, each deals 1d2 temporary Constitution damage per round unless the victim succeeds on a Fortitude save at DC 12 + the number of burrowed larvae. Removing each requires a DC 15 Heal check. Helpers risk the tendrils if the victim is still bound. Remove disease kills all larvae. They mature in two weeks.

gm.title: Description
lines: A medium hybrid creature fashioned by Simic Combine biomancers. Each specimen has one major and one minor adaptation.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The krasis can breathe air and water.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage.

gm.title: Creating a krasis
lines: Roll a d8 or choose once on each table. Apply one major and one minor adaptation to this base stat block before running the encounter.

gm.title: Major adaptations
lines:
1. Acidic Skin. A creature that touches the krasis or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft. takes 2 (1d4) acid damage.
2. Armored Hide. Natural plates or scales increase AC by 4, to 19.
3. Bioluminescent Markings. Runelike markings grant advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
4. Flight. Wings provide a flying speed equal to its walking speed (30 ft.).
5. Grabber. A creature hit by Claws is grappled by a specialized appendage (escape DC 13). The krasis can grapple only one creature this way at a time.
6. Hypnotic Display (Recharge 5–6). As an action, surround the krasis with shifting shapes and colors. Each creature within 15 ft. that can see it must make a DC 12 Wisdom save. On a failure, the creature is stunned for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. A successful save grants immunity to Hypnotic Display from any krasis for 24 hours.
7. Venomous Sting. A creature hit by Claws must pass a DC 12 Constitution save or become poisoned for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
8. Regeneration. At the start of each of its turns, the krasis regains 2 HP if it has at least 1 HP.

gm.title: Minor adaptations
lines:
1. Amorphous Structure. The krasis can pass through a 1-inch gap without squeezing.
2. Aquatic. A swimming speed equal to its walking speed (30 ft.).
3. Climbing Speed. A climbing speed equal to its walking speed (30 ft.).
4. Cryptic Skin. The krasis can shift its color to blend in. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide.
5. Heightened Awareness. Enhanced sensory organs prevent the krasis from being surprised.
6. Ink Cloud (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). While underwater, the krasis can spend a bonus action to release ink and then move up to its speed. The ink stays in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered on a point in the space the krasis occupied before moving. The sphere is heavily obscured until the ink disperses after 1 minute or a strong current clears it.
7. Leaping Legs. The krasis can long jump 20 ft. and high jump 10 ft., with or without a running start.
8. Stabilizing Legs. Extra crablike legs grant advantage on Strength and Dexterity saves against effects that would knock the krasis prone.

Claws. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 33 (6d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must make a DC 19 Strength save or fall prone.

gm.title: Creating a krasis
lines: Roll a d8 or choose once on each table. Apply one major and one minor adaptation to this base stat block before running the encounter.

gm.title: Major adaptations
lines:
1. Acidic Skin. A creature that touches the krasis or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft. takes 6 (1d12) acid damage.
2. Armored Hide. Natural plates or scales increase AC by 4, to 20.
3. Bioluminescent Markings. Runelike markings grant advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
4. Flight. Wings provide a flying speed equal to its walking speed (40 ft.).
5. Grabber. A creature hit by Claws is grappled by a specialized appendage (escape DC 19). The krasis can grapple only one creature this way at a time.
6. Hypnotic Display (Recharge 5–6). As an action, surround the krasis with shifting shapes and colors. Each creature within 15 ft. that can see it must make a DC 18 Wisdom save. On a failure, the creature is stunned for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. A successful save grants immunity to Hypnotic Display from any krasis for 24 hours.
7. Venomous Sting. A creature hit by Claws must pass a DC 18 Constitution save or become poisoned for 1 minute. It is also paralyzed while poisoned by this sting. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
8. Regeneration. At the start of each of its turns, the krasis regains 10 HP if it has at least 1 HP.

gm.title: Minor adaptations
lines:
1. Amorphous Structure. The krasis can pass through a 1-inch gap without squeezing.
2. Aquatic. A swimming speed equal to its walking speed (40 ft.).
3. Climbing Speed. A climbing speed equal to its walking speed (40 ft.).
4. Cryptic Skin. The krasis can shift its color to blend in. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide.
5. Heightened Awareness. Enhanced sensory organs prevent the krasis from being surprised.
6. Ink Cloud (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). While underwater, the krasis can spend a bonus action to release ink and then move up to its speed. The ink stays in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered on a point in the space the krasis occupied before moving. The sphere is heavily obscured until the ink disperses after 1 minute or a strong current clears it.
7. Leaping Legs. The krasis can long jump 40 ft. and high jump 30 ft., with or without a running start.
8. Stabilizing Legs. Extra crablike legs grant advantage on Strength and Dexterity saves against effects that would knock the krasis prone.

gm.title: Description
lines: A cave predator that lowers a sticky filament from walls or ceilings and reels in trapped prey.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces and move upside down on ceilings without an ability check.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Retract Filament. Choose one Large or smaller creature grappled by Adhesive Filament. It makes a DC 13 Strength save. On a failure, the cave fisher pulls it into an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of itself and makes one Claw attack against it. Retraction releases everyone else attached to the filament. The cave fisher cannot use Adhesive Filament until that target's grapple ends.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Adhesive Filament. Extend a sticky filament up to 60 ft. It adheres to anything that touches it. A creature caught by the filament is grappled (escape DC 13), with disadvantage on ability checks to escape. The filament has AC 15, 5 hit points, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. A weapon that attacks the filament and fails to sever it sticks. Freeing that weapon requires an action and a successful DC 13 Strength check. Destroying the filament leaves the cave fisher unharmed. Using Adhesive Filament again makes the old filament crumble.

gm.title: Description
lines: A foot-tall lizard kin ambusher. Caymas use hidden village entrances and prefer a quick strike followed by retreat.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Temperate to subtropical swamps or forests. Uncommon. Village of 10d6 adults and half as many noncombatants. Active at any time. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure K. Neutral. No magic resistance. Height about 1 foot. Morale 8–10.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack once for 1d3 damage or use a weapon. Bone daggers deal 1d2. A bok deals 1d6. Caymas use it two-handed as a pike and cannot throw it.
Ambush. A concealed cayma imposes a −2 penalty on the target’s surprise roll.

gm.title: Senses and skills
lines: Infravision 90 feet. Hide in Shadows and Move Silently each succeed 40% of the time. Speaks a Shazak dialect. Knowing one lizard kin dialect gives basic comprehension of the other two. A few individuals speak Common.

gm.title: Village shaman
lines: Each village has a shaman equivalent to a 5th- to 7th-level priest. The shaman has AC 6 and raises a party’s morale by one level. XP by Hit Dice, with Legacy value second. 5 HD 420 or 650 XP. 6 HD 650 or 975 XP. 7 HD 975 or 1,400 XP.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: A cayma entering the cursed lands can acquire a Legacy and needs cinnabryl to prevent Affliction. A standard cayma with a Legacy is worth 120 XP.

gm.title: Cayma grenades
lines:
A Wokan can supply ceramic grenades. On impact against a hard surface, roll 1d20. The grenade breaks and releases its cloud on 1–17.
Sleep. Within 1 foot of the impact, anyone whose head or breathing organ is in the cloud must save vs. breath weapon or sleep for 1d4 turns.
Choke. Same area and save as sleep. Failure leaves the victim unable to attack or defend for 1d6 rounds.
Fog. A 5-foot radius blocks ordinary vision and infravision for 1d6 rounds. Strong wind halves the duration.
Weapon details. Savage Coast Campaign Book, Part 2, pp. 136–137.

gm.title: Description
lines: The camel-headed Abomination looks after the others at camp. In a fight, Ceemal heals allies and draws them back out of danger.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Con +4, Int +5, Wis +6. Skills Medicine +6, Nature +5, Perception +6, Stealth +8, Survival +6. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 16. Common.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Octopodan Camouflage. Ceemal can try to Hide while lightly obscured by natural conditions such as foliage, mist, heavy rain, or snow.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Fillet Knife attacks or two Acid Spit attacks.
Fillet Knife. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage. If the target is a creature, another Abomination within 5 ft. of it heals for half the damage dealt.
Acid Spit. Ranged weapon attack +6, range 20/40 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) acid damage. The target is Poisoned until the start of Ceemal’s next turn.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: To Me, Sweetie (3/day). Choose an ally within 30 ft. who can hear Ceemal. The ally can spend its reaction to move up to its speed toward Ceemal without provoking opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Wail of Loss. When an enemy within 60 ft. reduces another Abomination Ceemal can see to 0 HP, the enemy makes a DC 14 Constitution save. It takes 7 (2d6) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Abominations. Once per encounter for each party action, after an enemy finishes its turn. The party can use the actions in any order, one per round. The creature performing the action must be present and must not be Incapacitated.
Action 3, All You Can Meat. Ceemal throws a piece of meat to every Abomination they can see within 30 ft. Each target that is not Incapacitated can eat the meat without spending an action and regain 8 (1d10 + 3) HP.

gm.title: Description
lines: Owl-eyed celestial bounty hunters judge whether the punishment a petitioner seeks fits the injury. A celebrun that takes a contract pursues its quarry with immortal patience.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Studded leather. Perception 16, Stealth 17. Resistant to radiant damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Immune to Blinded. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Celestial and Common. Telepathy 60 ft.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +3, Dex +7, Con +2, Int +1, Wis +6, Cha +3

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Celestial Resilience. Resistance to radiant damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical.
Seekers Sign. On hitting a creature with Talons or Golden Helm, the celebrun can mark it. It knows the target’s exact location whenever they share a plane. The mark ends when either dies or it marks a different creature.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Greatsword and one Talons attack, or two Golden Helm attacks.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 14 Dexterity save or be Blinded until the end of its next turn.
Golden Helm. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage.
Whirling Wheel (recharge 5–6). Every creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. Failure deals 14 (4d6) slashing plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage. Success halves both.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Horn of Heaven. Choose a visible non-Celestial creature within 60 ft. that hears the horn. On a failed DC 14 Charisma save, golden light outlines it for 1 minute, negating the benefits of Invisible and granting advantage to attacks against it. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: This vampire drains a pinned victim’s mind and uses the same lunar powers as a nosferatu.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Adapted from the printed fledgling nosferatu. Initiative +8. Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 22. BAB +3, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +4 melee (1d6 + 1), +1 rapier +8 melee (1d6 + 2, 18–20), or masterwork heavy crossbow +8 ranged (1d10, 19–20/×2).
Domination (Su). Standard action on a target within 30 ft. that the vampire can look at. Will DC 18 or dominate person at caster level 12.
Intelligence Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple and drain 1d4 Intelligence each round the pin holds. At Intelligence 0 or less the victim becomes catatonic. Use this in place of Blood Drain. The source describes the persistent Domination save as a Blood Drain rider and gives no new rider for this replacement.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to call 1d6 + 1 rat swarms, 1d4 + 1 bat swarms, or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/silver and magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +4, spider climb, undead traits. Gaseous form as a standard action at will, with indefinite duration and fly speed 20 ft. (perfect). Alternate Form can assume bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf form. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.
Lunar Regeneration. Direct moonlight converts past damage to nonlethal damage even after apparent death. Heal 3, 4, 6, or 8 per round in crescent, half, gibbous, or full moonlight, plus the age bonus. Fire, acid, and blessed or holy weapons deal normal damage. It can reattach severed limbs. It cannot regenerate a lost limb or recover nonlethal damage with its head detached.
Restful Sleep. While at 1 HP or more, heal 1 HP per HD per hour in its coffin. Daylight disables supernatural abilities. After exposure to direct sunlight, it must sleep in its coffin for 8 hours to restore them. Existing domination persists, and an alternate form cannot end until powers return.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: If a victim dies while its Intelligence is 0 or less from the drain, it rises under the creator’s control on the next full moon. A victim with 4 or fewer HD returns as spawn and one with 5 or more HD as a cerebral vampire. The creature regains its original Intelligence in undeath. Cerebral spawn also replace Blood Drain with Intelligence Drain. Nosferatu spawn retain charm, gaseous form, spider climb and daylight powerlessness. They heal 2 HP per hour asleep in their coffins if at 1 HP or more, or 2 HP per round in direct full moonlight.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines: Garlic repels it, and a clearly presented holy symbol or mirror keeps it 5 ft. away. It cannot enter a private home without invitation. A stake through the heart kills it while left in place. At 0 HP it collapses but may return in moonlight. Burn the whole body or scatter the severed limbs beyond its minions’ reach. Running water costs one-third of HP each round and destroys it after 3 rounds of immersion.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +21, Diplomacy +16, Gather Information +11, Hide +12, Intimidate +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Search +13, Sense Motive +15, Spot +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Diplomacy), Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter adaptation
lines: Apply the strain to the 3.5 vampire template. Retain unmodified abilities, size, BAB, saves and skill points. The base vampire uses undead d12 Hit Dice and has no Constitution score. Keep an existing swim speed and ignore vulnerability to immersion in running water if the base creature can swim. Use save DC 10 + half HD rounded down + Charisma modifier unless specified. Age rows replace one another. Nosferatu lack the base vampire’s Energy Drain. Age DR always requires silver and magic. The cerebral subtype changes the feeding attack only.

gm.title: Age modifiers
lines:
Apply one row to a base creature. The sample already includes its adjustments. Ability scores are listed in Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha order.
Fledgling. Abilities 4/4/2/2/6. Speed +0 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 10, lunar healing +0.
Mature. Abilities 4/4/4/2/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 15, lunar healing +0.

Eminent. Abilities 8/8/6/6/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +7, CR +4. DR 20, lunar healing +2.
Patriarch. Abilities 10/10/8/8/12. Speed +30 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +8, CR +5. DR 25, lunar healing +3.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid killed by energy drain rises as vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. One reduced to Constitution 0 by blood drain returns as spawn if it had 4 or fewer HD or as a chiang-shi if it had 5 or more. A creator controls its spawn until it dies.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines:
It avoids smoke made by burning rosemary and myrrh and cannot touch a creature wearing a rosemary and ivy garland. It cannot cross running water on its own. It can be carried over in a coffin or on a conveyance. It rests by day in a coffin lined with native soil. Scattering rosemary and myrrh on that soil bars it permanently from that coffin.
Direct sunlight leaves it with a single move or attack action. It is destroyed in the next round if it cannot escape the light. Immersion in running water takes away one-third of its HP each round and destroys it at the end of round 3. A vampire strain whose base creature has a swim speed retains it and escapes the immersion weakness.
At 1 HP or more it heals 5 HP per round. At 0 HP or less it turns invisible and intangible and flees without attacking. It is destroyed if it misses the 2-hour deadline to reach its coffin. After 1 hour there it reaches 1 HP and resumes healing.
A bamboo shaft through the heart kills it while the shaft remains in place. For permanent destruction, bless a rosemary blossom, put it in the vampire’s mouth, then sew its lips and eyes shut with a silver needle and golden thread.

Damage reduction in every tier requires bamboo and magic to bypass. Apply one age row only. The sample above already incorporates its age. gm.title: Appearance
lines: A winged guardian with three heads, a lion, a ram and a dragon, and a scaled tail.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor 13 + PB. Constitution save +2 + PB. Athletics +3 + PB. Immune to Frightened. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Bite). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Ram’s Defense (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack. A hit gives the target disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of the chimera’s next turn.
Level 3, Lion’s Leap (5 Ferocity). The chimera moves up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. If it ends on the ground, each creature within 5 ft. makes a Strength save against DC 10 + PB or falls Prone.
Level 5, Volcanic Blow (8 Ferocity). Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere around the point makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB. It takes PBd6 fire damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Protective Absorption (short or long rest). When the caregiver takes damage within 60 ft. of the chimera, the chimera can use its reaction to take half that damage in the caregiver’s place, rounded up.

gm.title: Mystic connection
lines: Defensive Eruption. At 9th level, a Beastheart with this companion and Mystic Connection can spend a bonus action once per long rest to unleash a burst of energy. Each enemy within 30 ft. makes a Dexterity save against the Beastheart’s exploit save DC. On a failure it takes 4d6 fire damage and falls Prone. On a success it takes half damage. The Beastheart and allies within 30 ft. have advantage on their next attack roll before the start of the Beastheart’s next turn.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A towering demon made from mismatched limbs, a violet crest, angular support legs, and several toothed maws.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Huge Fiend (Demon, Category 5), typically chaotic evil

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Str +11, Dex +5, Cha +5. Intimidation +9, Perception +6. Resists cold, fire, and thunder. Darkvision 120 ft., Soulsight 30 ft., passive Perception 16. Abyssal and Common. Telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Soul Resistance. With at least 2 souls, the chimeron has advantage on saving throws against powers, spells, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make up to three different attacks from Powerful Bite, Scorching Bite, Booming Bite, and Chilling Bite.
Powerful Bite. Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 25 (4d8 + 7) piercing damage.
Scorching Bite. Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing plus 9 (2d8) fire damage. The target catches fire and takes 7 (2d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. The target or a creature that can reach it can use an action to put out the flames. Reigniting the target does not stack the ongoing damage.
Booming Bite (1 soul). Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing plus 9 (2d8) thunder damage. The target falls Prone.
Chilling Bite (1 soul). Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing plus 9 (2d8) cold damage. The target’s speed is halved through the end of its next turn, and it can make only one attack during that turn.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Pain Absorption (1 soul). When it takes damage, the chimeron reduces that damage by 16 (3d10).

gm.title: MCDM demon soul rules
lines:
Soul count. Use the printed starting total or roll the listed dice. Souls spent on a feature are deducted from the total. A demon can accumulate souls without a maximum.
Soul Devourer. When the demon drops a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure, the demon consumes its soul, adds 1 to its soul count, and the creature dies. Only Wish can restore it to life.
Lethe. At 0 souls, the demon has advantage on attacks and disadvantage on saving throws, and its Intelligence is 3. On each turn it must use its movement to get as close as possible to the nearest creature it senses with Soulsight. If able, it must then use its action to attack that creature and attempt to kill it. It can pursue no other goal until its soul count rises.
Soulsight. Within the creature’s listed radius, it perceives creatures other than Constructs and Undead. This counts as seeing them for its features. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.
