gm.title: Description
lines: Chol armies hire pyrols as incendiary artillery. The fiends take payment in magic items that produce light or fire.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 14, Stealth 16. Resists cold, lightning, poison, and damage from nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing attacks. Resists Grappled, Poisoned, and Restrained. Immune to acid and fire damage and Charmed. Darkvision 60 ft. Speaks Abyssal, Common, and Infernal. Telepathy 60 ft.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: STR +3 · DEX +6 · CON +3 · INT +1 · WIS +1 · CHA +6

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Acidic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical and add 2d8 acid damage on a hit, as included below.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Stifling Heat. A non-Fiend that starts its turn within 10 ft. makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and deals half damage with Strength-based weapon attacks until its next turn starts. Failing by at least 5 also adds one level of Exhaustion. A creature can gain Exhaustion from this pyrol’s heat only once per 24 hours.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Claw or Clinging Flame.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 17 (4d6 + 3) slashing plus 9 (2d8) acid damage.
Clinging Flame. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 90 ft., one target. Hit 21 (4d8 + 3) fire damage. A creature or flammable object catches fire and takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until a creature uses an action to put out the fire.
Fiery Acid Burst (Recharge 5–6). Each creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. Failure deals 13 (3d8) acid and 13 (3d8) fire damage. Success halves each. A creature that fails by at least 5 takes another 4 (1d8) acid and 4 (1d8) fire damage at the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Burning Dash. Move up to half speed. The spaces crossed hold puddles of flaming acid until the start of the pyrol’s next turn. The first creature to enter a given puddle takes 2 (1d4) fire damage and extinguishes that puddle.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: A spiderlike cleric that snares foes in webs and attacks with a floating dagger.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fey Ancestry. The choldrith has advantage on saves against being charmed, and magic cannot put it to sleep.
Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces and move upside down on ceilings without an ability check.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
Web Sense. While touching a web, it knows the exact location of other creatures touching that same web.
Web Walker. Webbing does not restrict its movement.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one Large or smaller creature. On a hit, webbing restrains the target. The target can use an action to break the webbing with a successful DC 11 Strength check. The webbing can also be attacked. It has AC 10, 5 hit points, fire vulnerability, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one of the following spells with Wisdom (spell save DC 12).
At will. Guidance, Thaumaturgy.
1/day each. Bane, Hold Person.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Spectral Dagger (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Conjure a floating spectral dagger within 60 ft. The choldrith can make a melee spell attack (+4 to hit) against one creature within 5 ft. of the dagger. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) force damage. The dagger lasts 1 minute. On later turns, the choldrith can use a bonus action to move it up to 20 ft. and repeat the attack against one creature within 5 ft. of it.

gm.title: Description
lines: A shy nature spirit about six inches tall. It peers out from rocks, plants, and streams, sometimes following a traveler to see what they do with their tools.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would halve damage, the chwinga takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Unusual Nature. Chwingas sleep and need no air, food, or drink. When one dies, choose what remains: flower petals, a puff of pollen, a tiny statuette, a smooth stone, or fresh water.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: Innate Spellcasting. Wisdom is the chwinga’s spellcasting ability. It needs no verbal or material components. At will: Druidcraft, Guidance, Pass without Trace, Resistance.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Magical Gift (1/day). Choose a humanoid the chwinga can see within 5 ft. The DM chooses one supernatural charm for that humanoid.
Natural Shelter. Enter a rock, living plant, or natural source of fresh water in the chwinga’s space. Attacks, spells, and other effects cannot target it while it is sheltered, and its blindsight still works. It can emerge as an action. Destroying the shelter puts the unharmed chwinga in the shelter’s space.

gm.title: Charm of Restoration
lines: The chwinga in Nangalore’s eastern spirit dome can favor the tallest party member with this gift. It has 6 charges. As an action, spend 4 charges to cast Greater Restoration or 2 to cast Lesser Restoration. The charm disappears when its charges are spent.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 216–217. See p. 77 for Nangalore’s charm and p. 104 for the wagon encounter. Supernatural charms are in the Dungeon Master’s Guide (2014), chapter 7.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: In Omu, a chwinga shelters in a mossy disk beneath an overturned wagon. It comes out if travelers leave an offering or follows them secretly if they pass by. It favors curly hair or beards. Vegepygmies flee once they notice it with the party. It stays outside shrines and dungeons.

lines: Speed · 20 ft., climb 20 ft., swim 20 ft.

gm.title: Description
lines: A tiny spirit with a mask-like face. Astronauts make their homes on habitable moons and asteroids. Some stow away aboard ships or ride a Space Guppy.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Evasion. If a Dexterity save normally halves damage, the chwinga takes none on a success and half on a failure. This trait has no effect while the chwinga is incapacitated.
Unusual Nature. The chwinga needs no air, food, or drink. At death, the DM chooses what it becomes: moondust, sparkling spores, a likeness in miniature, a piece of ice, or a twelve-sided sponge.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Magical Gift (1/day). Bestow a supernatural charm of the DM’s choice on a visible Humanoid within 5 ft. See the Spelljammer charms below or the Dungeon Master’s Guide.
Natural Shelter. Enter a rock, bush, tree, or natural freshwater source located in the chwinga’s space. While sheltered, the chwinga retains its blindsight and cannot be targeted by attacks, spells, or other effects. It can emerge as an action. Destroying the shelter places the chwinga unharmed in the shelter’s space.
Spellcasting. Cast Druidcraft, Guidance, Pass without Trace, or Resistance at will using Charisma. The spells require no material or verbal components.

gm.title: Spelljammer charms
lines:
Charm of Air Bubbles. The recipient can cast Air Bubble as an action. They lose this charm after casting it three times.
Charm of Instant Tools. The recipient conjures one set of Artisan’s Tools, Navigator’s Tools, or Thieves’ Tools in hand or in their space. The charm ends after one use. The tools stay.

A creature that moves into it for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must pass a DC 16 Constitution save or take 10 (3d6) fire damage. The cloud lasts for 1 minute unless a strong wind disperses it sooner.

Condition immunities include Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained and Unconscious. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Searing Presence. A creature that starts its turn within 5 ft. of the elemental takes 5 (1d10) fire damage.
Molten Form. The elemental fits through openings as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing and can enter and remain in a hostile creature’s space. On its first entry into a creature’s space on a turn, the other creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage and makes a DC 14 Strength save. Failure leaves it Restrained. It takes another 5 (1d10) fire damage if it starts its turn Restrained by this trait. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to break free.
Water Susceptibility. It takes 1 cold damage for each 5 ft. it moves through water or each gallon splashed on it.

Molten Gaze. Ranged spell attack +8 against one target within 30 ft. A hit deals 21 (6d6) fire. The target also makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, the elemental destroys one nonmagical item of its choice that the target is carrying.

gm.title: Description
lines: A painted clay guardian of Shagambi’s shrine. It bears a bronze spear and a wooden shield, and returns to its cell when destroyed.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Climbing. It can climb difficult surfaces and ceilings without a check.
Steadfast. It cannot be disarmed or make ranged attacks.
Brute. Its melee weapon hits include an extra weapon damage die, already counted below.
Construct Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep and cannot speak.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks.
Spear. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) when wielded with two hands.
Shield Bash. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Parry. Add 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. It must see the attacker and hold a melee weapon.

gm.title: Shagambi’s shrine
lines: Four cells hold one guardian apiece. At least 50 lb. on the pit’s pressure plate raises the cell gates and calls the guardians. A gladiator fights if attacked or called to the pit. It cannot leave the shrine. At 0 HP outside the pit, it and its gear disappear and it immediately reforms in its cell at full health with spear and shield. It can then return to the pit. A gladiator destroyed in the pit leaves its spear behind as it reforms. If a spear leaves the shrine, it returns to the gladiator’s hand. When no other creatures remain inside, the gladiators return to their cells and the gates close. Place one spear from each guardian in the four warrior statues to free Shagambi’s puzzle cube.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 100. The shrine gives changes to the 2014 Gladiator stat block and separate reformation rules.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Damage Immunities acid, poison, psychic; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren’t adamantine Condition Immunities charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned Senses darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 9 Languages understands the languages of its creator but can’t speak

gm.title: Traits
lines: Acid Absorption. Whenever the golem is subjected to acid damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of hit points equal to the acid damage dealt. Berserk. Whenever the golem starts its turn with 60 hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points. Immutable Form. The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form. Magic Resistance. The golem has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Magic Weapons. The golem’s weapon attacks are magical.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The golem makes two slam attacks. Slam. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have its hit point maximum reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. The target dies if this attack reduces its hit point maximum to 0. The reduction lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. Haste (Recharge 5–6). Until the end of its next turn, the golem magically gains a +2 bonus to its AC, has advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and can use its slam attack as a bonus action.

gm.title: Description
lines: A clockwork bodyguard that wants to be human. Its flourishes keep opponents off balance, but each damaging strike spends some of the time left in its springs.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Very rare. Solitary. Active any time. No food. Very to exceptional intelligence (11–16). Fearless morale (19–20). Height 6 feet. No magic resistance. A destroyed automaton yields Q × 2 in gems and 1d4 × 1,000 gp in precious metal.

gm.title: Hit Dice, THAC0 and XP
lines:
5 HD: THAC0 15, 650 XP.
6 HD: THAC0 15, 975 XP.
7 HD: THAC0 13, 1,400 XP.
8 HD: THAC0 13, 2,000 XP.
9–10 HD: THAC0 11, adding 1,000 XP per HD above 8.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Weapons. Two attacks by weapon with +1 to hit and +3 damage for effective Strength 18. It usually carries a rapier and main-gauche or a saber and stiletto. There is a 20% chance it also has a wheellock pistol. Each point of damage it deals costs one hour of activity.
Additional action. Roll d100 each round. 01–25 fancy move, parry as a 10th-level fighter and improve AC by 6. 26–45 amusing quip, same parry and a taunt against one target. 46–60 salute or disarm. The salute gives allies +1 to attack for one round per Hit Die. 61–75 compliment, an opposite-sex target saves vs. spell or comes under charm person. 76–90 embarrassing maneuver, make a called shot at no penalty and follow a success with an amusing quip. 91–100 bold fencing attack, gain +2 to attack this round and force the foe back 1d10 steps. Ignore that last result when fewer than 50 hours remain.

gm.title: Skills and defenses
lines: Use the abilities and nonweapon proficiencies of a swashbuckler of level equal to HD, with no fighting school. Proficiency checks succeed on 18 or less. Immune to mind-influencing magic such as charm person and suggestion. ESP and telepathy can still affect it. If exposed to moisture, save vs. poison or take 6d6 damage 1d4 days later. It fears rust monsters.

gm.title: Winding
lines: Maximum runtime is 10 hours per HP, then it goes dormant. Roll d100 for the percentage remaining when encountered, with a 10% minimum. Below 50%, it heads back to its creator. Rewinding restores one hour per round. Attempting to wind it fully has a 10% chance of destroying it. Only its creator can repair it, and it cannot be raised. It cannot rewind itself. Models of at least 9 HD often need a magical key kept by their maker.

gm.title: Variants
lines: A host to a heroic spirit can rewind itself upon obtaining its key. The spirit can stay until the mechanism rusts. A rogue automaton hosts a legacy leech, can rewind without a key, and uses effective Strength 19. It keeps its swashbuckler abilities and can use Legacies its symbiont shares. Ordinary swordsmen neither gain Legacies nor require cinnabryl.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The 46–60 result lists disarm as an option without adding a special disarm procedure.

gm.title: Description
lines: A cloud giant lays wagers against rivals across the planes and wears a runic half mask that cuts through magical trickery.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Cloud Rune. A mask in the giant’s possession bears the rune. While holding or wearing it, the giant has truesight out to 30 ft. and can use Thunderous Clap and Negate Spell. The mask has AC 15, 45 HP, and immunity to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It recovers all its HP at the end of every turn. It turns to dust at 0 HP or when the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe it on a mask it possesses when it finishes a short or long rest.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Flying Staff attacks.
Flying Staff. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. or range 30/90 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 18 (3d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 16 (3d10) thunder damage. The staff magically returns to the giant’s hand immediately after a ranged attack, hit or miss.
Thunderous Clap (requires Cloud Rune). Magically summon a thundercloud in a 30-ft.-radius sphere around a visible point within 60 ft. It spreads around corners. Each creature in the cloud makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure deals 52 (8d12) thunder damage and knocks the creature prone. Success halves the damage and avoids being knocked prone. The clap is audible 300 ft. from the center. The cloud heavily obscures the area until the start of the giant’s next turn or until strong wind disperses it.
Spellcasting. Cast one listed spell without material components, using Charisma (save DC 20).
At will. Detect Magic, Fog Cloud, Light, Minor Illusion.
1/day each. Dream (as an action), Gaseous Form, Major Image.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Negate Spell (requires Cloud Rune). When the giant sees a creature within 60 ft. casting a spell, it can interrupt the casting. A spell cast with a slot of 3rd level or lower fails. For a spell of 4th level or higher, the caster must pass a DC 18 Intelligence save or the spell fails.

gm.title: Optional wager spells
lines: For a giant that has won a wager for spellcasting power, add one or more of Circle of Death, Harm, Otiluke’s Freezing Sphere, and Sunbeam to Spellcasting. Each added spell is usable once per day.

gm.title: Description
lines: A cloud giant trickster who changes shape, controls the weather, and strikes with telekinetic force.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Control Weather (8th-level spell). The giant can cast Control Weather with Charisma and needs no material components.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks or two Telekinetic Strike attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (1d10) psychic damage.
Telekinetic Strike. Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 240 ft., one target. A hit deals 25 (4d10 + 3) force damage.
Change Shape. The giant magically takes on the appearance and feel of a Beast or Humanoid it has seen, or returns to its true form. The new form absorbs any equipment the giant wears or carries. Its size can change, and it keeps its other statistics. Death returns the giant to its true form.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 15). These spells require no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Fog Cloud, Light, Minor Illusion.
3/day each. Invisibility, Silent Image, Suggestion, Tongues.
1/day each. Gaseous Form, Major Image.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Cloud Step (Recharge 4–6). Teleport up to 60 ft. to an unoccupied space the giant can see, taking all worn and carried equipment.

Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +12 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage. Add 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage if the giant had advantage on the attack roll.
Change Shape. The giant magically becomes a Beast or Humanoid it has seen, or returns to its true form. Its equipment merges with the new form. Size is the only statistic that changes. It returns to its true form when it dies.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lodestone-powered construct that guards the most restricted archives of the Cobalt Soul.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Immune to fire, lightning, poison and psychic damage. Immune to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons that are not adamantine. Immune to Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified and Poisoned. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 10. Understands its creator’s languages but cannot speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Immutable Form. Effects and spells cannot change the golem’s shape.
Magic Resistance. It rolls saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical.
Conductive Body. Lightning causes no damage. Instead, through the end of the golem’s next turn, its weapon attacks deal an extra 11 (2d10) lightning damage. In that window, a creature takes 11 (2d10) lightning damage if it touches the golem or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Slam and Sword, or use Magnetic Pulse followed by Spinning Cleave.
Slam. Melee weapon attack +15 within 5 ft. Hit for 25 (3d10 + 9) bludgeoning.
Sword. Melee weapon attack +15 within 10 ft. Hit for 28 (3d12 + 9) slashing.
Spinning Cleave. Make a Sword attack against every creature within 10 ft.
Magnetic Pulse (recharge 6). Unattended metal objects within 30 ft. are pulled into unoccupied spaces within 5 ft. of the golem. A creature within 30 ft. that is made of metal or wearing metal armor must pass a DC 20 Strength save or be pulled into an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the golem and knocked Prone.

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Traits
lines: Berserk. At the start of a turn when the cobblefright has 40 HP or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6 it goes berserk. While berserk, it attacks the nearest creature it can see each turn. If it cannot move to and attack a creature, it attacks an object, preferring one smaller than itself. It stays berserk until destroyed or restored to full HP.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Claw attacks. One may be replaced by Grab.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Grab. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature the cobblefright is not already grappling. On a hit the creature is Grappled (escape DC 15). The cobblefright can hold up to two creatures. At the start of its turn, it can squeeze each creature held, once per target. Each squeezed creature must pass a DC 15 Strength save or take 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Soul Siphon. One creature held by the cobblefright makes a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 11 (2d10) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. Reduce the target's hit point maximum by the necrotic damage dealt and restore the same number of hit points to the cobblefright. The reduction lasts until the target completes a short or long rest.

Success halves the damage and avoids Frightened. A Frightened target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. For each Beast or creature with the Animal tag and an Intelligence modifier of −3 or less, the colláis chooses whether it automatically fails or is immune to the effect.

lines: Toss. Choose one Medium or smaller creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 16 Strength save. Failure throws it up to 20 ft. away in a random direction and knocks it Prone.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: Faithful artisans build these towering figures in honor of their gods. A divine power can awaken the crystal in a colossus's heart and send it to defend the faithful or carry out the deity's will. Many lie dormant in remote places.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Understands Celestial and Common, and can't speak.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Stunned, Unconscious.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Immutable Form. The colossus can't shape-shift.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). When it fails a saving throw, the colossus can spend a use to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The colossus has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using Slam or Radiant Ray in any combination.
Slam. Melee attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) Bludgeoning damage and pushes the target up to 20 ft. directly away from the colossus.
Radiant Ray. Ranged attack, +18 to hit, range 300 ft. A hit deals 22 (4d10) Radiant damage. A Large or smaller creature hit also falls Prone.
Divine Beam (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 300-ft.-long, 10-ft.-wide Line make a DC 26 Dexterity save. The beam deals 65 (10d12) Radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 HP, it disintegrates into dust. The magic items it wore or carried remain.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses. The colossus can spend one use on an option immediately after another creature's turn. It cannot do so while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Smite. Make one Radiant Ray attack.
Stomp. Move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The colossus can make one Slam attack at any point during this move.

gm.title: Description
lines: A bronze-and-iron golem stands on twin plinths above the road to Akros. In a crisis, priests of Purphoros awaken it to defend the city.

gm.title: Damage immunities

gm.title: Condition immunities

gm.title: Languages

lines:
Constructed Nature. This construct needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Crumbling Destruction. At 0 HP, the colossus crumbles and is destroyed. Each creature on the ground within 30 ft. makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. A creature takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning plus 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
Fire Absorption. When fire would damage the colossus, it instead regains HP equal to that fire damage.
Immutable Form. Spells and effects can't alter its form.
Magic Weapons. The colossus's weapon attacks are magical.
Siege Monster. The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft. or range 200/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (4d6 + 9) piercing damage, or 27 (4d8 + 9) if wielded with two hands for a melee attack. The spear magically returns after a ranged attack.
Sword. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (6d8 + 9) slashing damage.
Flames of Akros (Recharge 6). Choose up to three visible creatures within 90 ft. Each makes a DC 24 Dexterity save against the magical flames. On a failure, it takes 36 (8d8) fire damage and catches fire for 1 minute. On a success, it takes half damage and doesn't catch fire. A burning creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, taking 18 (4d8) fire damage on a failure or ending the effect on a success.

lines:

lines:

gm.title: Description
lines: A copper dragon can become a greatwyrm by bringing together counterparts across worlds. It can breathe acid or release a cone of sapping gas.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Metallic Awakening (recharges after a short or long rest). When the creature would drop to 0 HP, set its current HP to 450, recharge Breath Weapon, and restore all spent uses of Legendary Resistance. The creature can take mythic actions for the following hour. Award 120,000 extra XP if defeated after this trait activates (240,000 XP total).
Legendary Resistance (4/day). Turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 20) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can hold only one creature with this attack at a time.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Breath Weapon (recharge 5–6). Choose Elemental Breath or Sapping Breath.
Elemental Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 84 (13d12) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sapping Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Constitution save. A failure leaves the creature unconscious for 1 minute. An unconscious creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds on the first save has disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of the greatwyrm’s next turn.
Change Shape. Magically take the form of any Medium or Small creature, retaining the greatwyrm’s statistics except size. The form ends if the greatwyrm drops to 0 HP or spends an action to end it.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The creature has 3 legendary actions. It can take one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains spent actions at the start of its turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its flying speed.

gm.title: Mythic actions
lines:
For 1 hour after Metallic Awakening activates, the greatwyrm can spend legendary actions on these options.
Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Shattering Roar (2 actions). Each creature in a 120-ft.-radius sphere centered on the greatwyrm must succeed on a DC 26 Constitution save or take 19 (3d12) thunder damage and be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Dragon customization
lines: Customize the dragon’s languages or skills to suit its history. Skill changes can include double proficiency or tool proficiencies. Use the optional innate spellcasting guidance for the dragon’s color when adding magic. Other options on p. 34 include alternate senses and the Change Shape, Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation, and Tunneler traits or actions.

gm.title: Description
lines: A climbing plant that gathers humanoid corpses to feed on or raise as zombies.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Corpses. When first encountered, the flower holds 1d6 + 3 Humanoid corpses, up to its capacity of nine. These corpses have total cover against attacks and other effects coming from outside the flower. If the flower dies, the corpses can be pulled free.
Spider Climb. The flower climbs difficult surfaces, including ceilings upside down, without making an ability check.
Stench of Death. A creature that starts its turn within 10 ft. of the flower or one of its zombies makes a DC 14 Constitution save. Constructs and Undead are exempt. On a failure, the creature is poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a success, it is immune to Stench of Death from all corpse flowers for 24 hours.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
Harvest the Dead. Swallow one unsecured Humanoid corpse within 10 ft. and everything it is wearing or carrying.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Digest. Destroy one corpse stored in the flower and immediately regain 11 (2d10) hit points. The flower expels the corpse's equipment into its own space.
Reanimate. Raise one stored corpse as a Zombie in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the flower. The zombie acts immediately after the flower in initiative and is its ally. The flower can't control the zombie. It carries the flower's Stench of Death.

gm.title: Description
lines: A corpse flower can sprout over a necromancer's grave or the remains of powerful undead. Once it uproots itself, it searches graveyards and battlefields for bodies.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Corpses. When first encountered, the flower contains 1d6 + 3 humanoid corpses. It can hold up to nine. Stored corpses have total cover against attacks and effects outside the flower. If the flower dies, the corpses can be pulled free.
Spider Climb. The flower can climb difficult surfaces and move upside down on ceilings without an ability check.
Stench of Death. When a creature other than a construct or undead starts its turn within 10 ft. of the flower or one of its zombies, it makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it is incapacitated until the end of that turn. Immunity to poison damage or the poisoned condition makes the save an automatic success. A creature that succeeds is immune to the stench of all corpse flowers for 24 hours.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage. The target must then make a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 14 (4d6) poison damage on a failure.
Harvest the Dead. Take one unsecured humanoid corpse within 10 ft. into the flower's body, together with anything it wears or carries. The flower can use the remains for its Corpses trait.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
The flower can choose one of the following options while it contains at least one humanoid corpse.
Digest. Consume a stored corpse to regain 11 (2d10) hit points immediately. The body is destroyed and its equipment drops into the flower's space.
Animate. Turn a stored corpse into a Zombie in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. The zombie acts directly after the flower in initiative and allies with it. The flower has no control over the zombie, which carries the flower's Stench of Death.

gm.title: Field notes
lines: After the flower dies, the smell of decay fades over 2d4 days.

lines: Innate Spellcasting. The couatl’s spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14). The couatl’s weapon attacks are magical. Shielded Mind. The couatl is immune to scrying and to any effect that would sense its emotions, read its thoughts, or detect its location.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 24 hours. Until this poison ends, the target is unconscious. Another creature can use an action to shake the target awake. Constrict. Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the couatl can’t constrict another target. Change Shape. The couatl magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating equal to or less than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the couatl’s choice). In a new form, the couatl retains its game statistics and ability to speak, but its AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and other actions are replaced by those of the new form, and it gains any statistics and capabilities (except class features, legendary actions, and lair actions) that the new form has but that it lacks. If the new form has a bite attack, the couatl can use its bite in that form.

lines:
Beguile. Pick one visible creature within 30 ft. that can see Rhodar. On a failed DC 20 Wisdom save, the target spends its reaction, if available, to move up to its speed to a location Rhodar chooses. Rhodar chooses whether it then falls Prone or makes a melee attack against a target he picks.
Inhuman Agility. Move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Withering Stare. When a visible creature within 60 ft. hits Rhodar, that creature makes a DC 20 Wisdom save or takes 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Use each villain action once per encounter after an enemy's turn. Use at most one per round, in any order.
Action 1, Bloodstained. Center a 20-ft.-radius sphere on a point Rhodar sees within 120 ft. Each creature there other than an Undead makes a DC 20 Dexterity save. On a failure, it is bloodstained until the end of Rhodar's next turn. He has advantage on attacks against it, and it has disadvantage on saves against his Beguile.
Action 2, Fire Drake. Rhodar and his gear turn into a Large dragon of fire. He releases any creature he is grappling and any Grappled or Restrained effect on him ends. He flies up to twice his speed to an unoccupied space, ignoring difficult terrain and opportunity attacks and able to pass through creatures and objects. Each creature he passes through makes a DC 20 Dexterity save, taking 36 (8d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. He then returns to his previous form.
Action 3, Mist of Blades. The area within 60 ft. is heavily obscured for other creatures. Rhodar can teleport up to four times to unoccupied spaces in the mist. After each teleport he can make one Sanguinus attack. The mist disappears at the end of the action.

gm.title: Utility Spells
lines: Charisma, save DC 20. At will, 1 action each: Charm Person, Detect Thoughts, Disguise Self, Sending. 3/day each, longer casting times: Clairvoyance, Geas (9th level), Legend Lore.

gm.title: Lair Actions
lines:

Blood Rain. Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Blood falls there in a 10-ft.-radius, 40-ft.-high cylinder until the end of initiative count 20 of the next round. A creature other than an Undead that takes necrotic damage while inside takes an extra 5 (1d10) necrotic damage.
Obey My Desire. Each creature within 60 ft. that hears the vampire makes a DC 18 Wisdom save or is Charmed until the end of this turn. Each creature Charmed this way immediately spends its reaction, if available, to make a melee attack against another creature, make one against itself, or fall Prone. The vampire picks the effect.

gm.title: Description
lines: A persistent cloud tower holds a sleeping scion. Disturb it and the cloud takes the shape of a towering wind elemental.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle dissipates into wisps of cloud. Scion of Memnor immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke an opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Slam and Wind Javelin.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 31 (4d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 19 (3d12) thunder damage.
Wind Javelin. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 27 (4d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) thunder damage. The target must pass a DC 25 Strength save or fall prone.
Vortex (recharge 5–6). Center a cylinder 30 ft. in radius and 100 ft. high on a visible point within 90 ft. Each creature other than the cradle inside makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 71 (11d12) bludgeoning damage and restrains the creature in the vortex. Success halves the damage and pushes the creature to the nearest unoccupied space outside the cylinder. The vortex lasts until the start of the cradle’s next turn. Creatures still restrained by it fall prone when it ends.
A creature restrained by the vortex can use an action to attempt a DC 19 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. On success, it escapes and moves 3d6 × 10 ft. away in a random direction.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Thunderclap. Immediately after taking damage, the cradle can force every other creature in a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on itself to make a DC 25 Constitution save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) thunder damage and deafens the creature for 1 minute.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Memnor can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 22 (3d8 + 9) piercing damage. A Large or smaller target must pass a DC 19 Dexterity save or be swallowed. A swallowed creature is Blinded and Restrained, has total cover against effects outside the wurm, and takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the wurm's turns. If a creature inside deals at least 30 damage to the wurm in one turn, the wurm makes a DC 21 Constitution save at that turn's end. On a failure it expels all swallowed creatures, which land Prone within 10 ft. A creature inside a dead wurm is no longer Restrained and can spend 20 ft. of movement to leave the corpse and land Prone.
Breach. The wurm uses its full movement and can enter the spaces of Large or smaller creatures. Whenever it enters a creature's space, that creature makes a DC 19 Strength save. On success, the creature can choose to be moved to the side of the wurm's space. On failure, or if it succeeds and declines that movement, it takes 35 (10d6) bludgeoning damage, is pushed 10 ft., and falls Prone. gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

Dispersed Vines (Ex). Cover one 5-by-5-ft. square per HD, on the ground or on a wall. Track each die’s HP separately. A section at 0 HP or with a comparable loss such as a negative level cannot act. At −10 HP it is destroyed. An area attack deals full damage to every section it reaches.
Berries (Ex). Autumn berries can establish new colonies. They produce 2d8 flowers per HD. Press one flower to a wound to stabilize a dying creature or stop bleeding. Each flower works once and can also be used to make a curing potion.

gm.title: Age tiers
lines:
1. Hatchling, 0–5 years. 7 HD, AC 0, THAC0 13, combat modifier +1. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure none, 2,000 XP. Body 2–16 ft., tail 4–16 ft.
2. Very Young, 6–15 years. 9 HD, AC -1, THAC0 11, combat modifier +2. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure none, 3,000 XP. Body 16–27 ft., tail 16–25 ft.
3. Young, 16–25 years. 11 HD, AC -2, THAC0 9, combat modifier +3. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure B, 5,000 XP. Body 27–42 ft., tail 25–34 ft.
4. Juvenile, 26–50 years. 13 HD, AC -3, THAC0 7, combat modifier +4. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure BI, 8,000 XP. Body 42–61 ft., tail 34–53 ft.
5. Young Adult, 51–100 years. 14 HD, AC -4, THAC0 7, combat modifier +5. Fear 15 yd., save +3. Magic resistance 20%. Spells none. Treasure BI, 10,000 XP. Body 61–80 ft., tail 53–72 ft.
6. Adult, 101–200 years. 15 HD, AC -5, THAC0 5, combat modifier +6. Fear 20 yd., save +2. Magic resistance 25%. Spells 1 wizard. Treasure BH, 12,000 XP. Body 80–99 ft., tail 72–91 ft.
7. Mature Adult, 201–400 years. 16 HD, AC -6, THAC0 5, combat modifier +7. Fear 25 yd., save +1. Magic resistance 30%. Spells 2 wizard. Treasure BH, 13,000 XP. Body 99–118 ft., tail 91–110 ft.
8. Old, 401–600 years. 17 HD, AC -7, THAC0 5, combat modifier +8. Fear 30 yd., save +0. Magic resistance 35%. Spells 2/1 wizard. Treasure BHU, 14,000 XP. Body 118–137 ft., tail 110–129 ft.
9. Very Old, 601–800 years. 18 HD, AC -8, THAC0 5, combat modifier +9. Fear 35 yd., save −1. Magic resistance 40%. Spells 2/2 wizard. Treasure BHU, 15,000 XP. Body 137–157 ft., tail 129–148 ft.
10. Venerable, 801–1,000 years. 19 HD, AC -9, THAC0 5, combat modifier +10. Fear 40 yd., save −2. Magic resistance 45%. Spells 2/2/1 wizard, 1 priest. Treasure BH + U × 2, 16,000 XP. Body 157–177 ft., tail 148–168 ft.
11. Wyrm, 1,001–2,000 years. 20 HD, AC -10, THAC0 5, combat modifier +11. Fear 45 yd., save −3. Magic resistance 50%. Spells 2/2/2 wizard, 2 priest. Treasure BH + U × 2, 18,000 XP. Body 177–197 ft., tail 168–188 ft.
12. Great Wyrm, 1,200+ years. 21 HD, AC -11, THAC0 5, combat modifier +12. Fear 50 yd., save −4. Magic resistance 55%. Spells 3/2/2/1 wizard, 2/1 priest. Treasure BH + U × 3, 20,000 XP. Body 197–217 ft., tail 188–208 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws and bite. Two claws at 1d8 each and a bite at 4d6. Add the age tier’s combat modifier to each physical damage roll. Claws can strike the front and sides, and the bite also reaches behind. The dragon saves as a fighter of level equal to HD.
Cinnabryl breath. From Juvenile onward, the dragon can breathe once every three rounds, giving up its other attacks that round. It produces a 100-foot cone measuring 5 feet wide at its mouth and 50 feet across at the far end. It depletes all cinnabryl and ruins crimson essence in the cone. The dragon has a cumulative 3% chance per ounce depleted to gain one new Legacy. The cone does not increase with age.

gm.title: Other dragon attacks
lines:
Kick. Against a target behind it, deal claw damage. The target rolls Dexterity or lower on 1d20 or is pushed 1d6 feet plus 1 foot per age tier. A pushed target saves vs. petrification with the combat modifier as a penalty or falls. Use one hind leg if also attacking with a claw. No tail slap in the same round.
Snatch. From Young Adult, dive to grab a target at least two sizes smaller. On a hit there is a 50% chance of pinning its arms. The dragon can drop it, deal automatic claw damage each round, or transfer it to its jaws with another successful attack roll for automatic bite damage each round. Old dragons can snatch two targets. Wyrms and Great Wyrms can carry three by transferring one to the mouth.
Wing buffet. From Young Adult, deal claw damage against a target at either side. It falls unless it rolls at or below Dexterity on 1d20.
Tail slap. From Adult, attack up to the age-tier number of targets at the rear and sides, rolling separately. Each hit deals twice claw damage, and the target saves vs. petrification at a penalty equal to the combat modifier or is stunned for 1d4 + 1 minutes. It can smash light wood or drain a cube of force by one charge per two points of combat modifier, rounded down.
Stall. Hover one round near the ground, then land. During the stall, the dragon can attack with all four legs and its bite, or breathe instead. Debris creates a dust cloud out to the fear radius for one round in suitable terrain. Anyone in it is blinded and cannot cast.
Optional plummet. From at least 30 feet above the target, land on up to the combat-modifier number of targets, rolling separately for bite damage. Each hit target saves vs. petrification at a penalty equal to the modifier or is pinned and takes the damage again on the next round if the dragon holds it down. It must save again to escape an ongoing pin. The dragon cannot do anything else while plummeting or holding the pin.

gm.title: Fear and spellcasting
lines:
From Young Adult, seeing it causes targets under 1 HD and nonaggressive noncarnivores below the dragon’s HD to panic for 4d6 rounds. Other creatures below its HD in a charging dragon’s fear radius or under its flight path at up to 250 feet altitude save vs. petrification with the listed modifier. Failure gives −2 to attack and damage. Creatures at least equal to its HD are immune.
Determine its spells from the age tier. A dragon generally casts each spell once per day or more if rolled more than once. Casting is verbal only with casting time 1. It cannot attack, breathe, use innate magic, or do more than glide while casting.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: The first Legacy requires the dragon to drain at least 1 ounce of cinnabryl with its breath. Juvenile and older dragons are assumed to have 1d4 − 1 random Legacies for each age category from Juvenile onward. Duplicate Legacies stack if possible. Otherwise roll again. Add 1,000 XP per Legacy. A new Legacy costs no ability points. Physical changes appear over a few days, and the dragon can reverse them over the following week.

gm.title: Harvested scales
lines: One hide yields enough cinnabryl-bearing scales for at most one set of armor. A crimson essence alchemist must treat the scales into scale mail using at least one potion of crimson essence. It protects only the wearer. A slashing, piercing, or magical hit dealing more than 15 damage calls for an appropriate item saving throw. On failure the scales lose their protection in a smokepowder-like detonation.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Choose an age tier before play. The printed Wyrm and Great Wyrm age ranges overlap.

The spell totals list slots by spell level. The appendix gives no direct HP damage for the cinnabryl breath. General dragon attacks, fear, and casting follow the Monstrous Manual, Dragons, General. THAC0 uses Dungeon Master Guide Table 39.

lines: Traces of the greatwyrm’s many lives across the Material Plane come together in a body that gleams like cut crystal.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Gem Awakening (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 hit points, it instead resets to 400 hit points, recharges Breath Weapon and recovers all spent Legendary Resistance uses. It can use Mass Telekinesis for the next hour. Defeating it after Gem Awakening grants an extra 90,000 XP, or 180,000 XP total.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The greatwyrm can turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing damage plus 16 (3d10) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d8 + 9) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 19) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can grapple only one creature this way at a time.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. A failure deals 71 (11d12) force damage and knocks the creature prone. A success halves the damage. The creature’s speed is 0 until the end of its next turn on either result.
Mass Telekinesis (Gem Awakening Only, Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Choose any number of visible creatures or objects within 120 ft., each weighing at most 4,000 lb. Worn or carried objects are ineligible. Each chosen creature must pass a DC 26 Strength save or be restrained in the greatwyrm’s grip. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, escaping on a success. At the end of each of the greatwyrm’s turns, it can move each target still in its grip up to 60 ft. in any direction, within 120 ft. of itself. It can also deal 45 (7d12) force damage to each restrained creature it chooses.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 26, +18 to hit) and requiring no components. Dispel Magic, Forcecage, Plane Shift, Reverse Gravity and Time Stop are each usable once per day.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Change Shape. Magically take the shape of a Small or Medium creature. Only size changes. The transformation ends when the greatwyrm drops to 0 hit points or spends a bonus action to end it.
Psychic Step. Magically teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 ft.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The greatwyrm has three legendary actions and recovers spent actions at the start of its turn. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Psychic Beam (3 actions). Each creature in a 90-ft. line 10 ft. wide makes a DC 26 Intelligence save, taking 27 (5d10) psychic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Dancing Flowers. The Dancing Lady has three flowers that look like life-sized dancers. Track each separately at AC 16 and 5 HP, with fire vulnerability, psychic immunity, and disadvantage on attacks against it. Destroying a flower leaves the Dancing Lady’s HP intact. Destroyed flowers regrow at the end of the Dancing Lady’s turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, 10-ft. reach, one target. Hit 25 (3d12 + 6) bludgeoning.
Blood-Red Waltz. For each remaining flower, choose up to one visible creature within 60 ft. of the Dancing Lady. Each target makes a DC 17 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 18 (4d8) psychic damage and the Dancing Lady moves it to an unoccupied space within 60 ft. of itself. On a success, it takes half damage and stays in place.
Disarming Quickstep. For each remaining flower, choose up to one visible creature within 60 ft. of the Dancing Lady. Each target makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 17 (5d6) bludgeoning damage and is Dazed until the start of the Dancing Lady’s next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and avoids Dazed.
Ballet of Terror (1/day). Each enemy within 120 ft. that can smell the flowers’ mist makes a DC 17 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is Frightened of the Dancing Lady for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Somber Dirge. When a visible attacker hits the Dancing Lady, redirect the hit to one of its flowers.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn, a Dazed creature chooses one of moving, taking an action, or taking a bonus action. If it becomes Dazed on its own turn, that turn ends. Extra actions such as those from Haste or Action Surge still apply. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can end the condition.

gm.title: Description
lines: A dao is a genie from the Elemental Plane of Earth. It reshapes rock into winding halls and bargains for treasure. When it flies, swirling sand takes the place of its legs.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Earth Glide. The dao can burrow through unworked nonmagical earth and stone without disturbing either.
Elemental Demise. When the dao dies, its body becomes crystalline powder. Its worn and carried equipment remains.
Sure-Footed. The dao rolls Strength and Dexterity saves against being knocked Prone with advantage.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines:
The dao uses Charisma, with save DC 14 and +6 to hit with spell attacks. Its spells require no material components.
At will. Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Stone Shape.
3/day each. Passwall, Move Earth, Tongues.
1/day each. Conjure Elemental (Earth Elemental only), Gaseous Form, Invisibility, Phantasmal Killer, Plane Shift, Wall of Stone.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Fist attacks or two Maul attacks.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Maul. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 20 (4d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit by the attack falls Prone unless it succeeds on a DC 18 Strength check.

gm.title: Statistics
lines: Speed · 30 ft., burrow 30 ft., fly 30 ft. (hover)

gm.title: Description
lines: An earth genie that glides through unworked stone and bargains for gems, metalwork, or fossils.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Earth Glide. The dao can burrow through unworked, nonmagical earth and stone without disturbing it.
Elemental Restoration. If the genie dies outside the Elemental Plane of Earth, its body dissolves into dirt. It returns at full HP in a new body somewhere on that plane after 1d4 days.
Magic Resistance. Roll saving throws against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
Wishes. Roll a 30 percent chance that this genie knows Wish. It can cast the spell solely on behalf of a non-genie who expresses a wish it understands. Casting this way causes the genie no stress from the spell. After three castings, it must wait 365 days before casting Wish again.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Earthen Maul attacks or two Earth Burst attacks.
Earthen Maul. Melee attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 20 (4d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage and knocks a Large or smaller creature Prone.
Earth Burst. Ranged attack, +10 to hit, range 120 ft. A hit deals 15 (2d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. Hit or miss, a blast erupts from the target's space. The target and each other creature in the 10-ft. Emanation centered there make a DC 16 Dexterity save. A failed save deals 10 (3d6) thunder damage.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Spellcasting. As an action, cast one listed spell with Charisma and no Material components. Spell save DC 16.
At will. Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Stone Shape.
1/day each. Gaseous Form, Invisibility, Move Earth, Passwall, Plane Shift, Tongues, Wall of Stone.

lines: Death Burn. When the elder dies, its body and possessions burn to ash, with metal and magic objects surviving. Magical light flashes out to 10 ft., and every creature in that radius makes a DC 11 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 7 (2d6) radiant damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn if it can see the flash. A successful save halves the damage and avoids the blindness.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.

gm.title: Description
lines: A cave hunter that clings to rock formations and drops over its prey before cloaking the area in darkness.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Echolocation. The darkmantle loses the use of its blindsight while Deafened.
False Appearance. A motionless darkmantle passes for a cave formation such as a stalactite or stalagmite.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Crush. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the darkmantle attaches. If the target is Medium or smaller and the darkmantle had advantage, it engulfs the target's head. That creature is Blinded and cannot breathe while its head is engulfed. While attached, the darkmantle moves with the target. Its speed becomes 0, speed bonuses have no effect, and it can attack only the target, with advantage. A creature can take an action and succeed on a DC 13 Strength check to remove it. The darkmantle can detach on its turn by spending 5 ft. of movement.
Darkness Aura (1/Day). Magical darkness spreads around corners in a 15-ft. radius from the darkmantle and moves with it. The darkness lasts up to 10 minutes while the darkmantle maintains Concentration as if on a spell. Darkvision cannot see through it, and natural light cannot illuminate it. If it overlaps light created by a spell of 2nd level or lower, that spell is dispelled.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: A hit attaches it. It can attach to a Medium or smaller head, blinding the victim and blocking breathing. The victim or another creature can remove it with a DC 13 Strength check. Its darkness aura is available once per day and requires concentration.

gm.title: Description
lines: This ceiling hunter resembles a stalactite until it drops and spreads its webbed tentacles over its prey.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Crush. Melee attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. On a hit, deal 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage and attach to the target. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature and the darkmantle had Advantage on the attack roll, it covers the target. The covered creature is Blinded and suffocates until the darkmantle detaches. While attached, the darkmantle can attack only the target and has Advantage on its attacks. Its Speed becomes 0, and bonuses cannot increase it. It moves with the target. A creature can take an action to detach the darkmantle from itself with a successful DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check. The darkmantle can spend 5 ft. of movement on its own turn to detach.
Darkness Aura (1/day). Magical Darkness fills a 15-ft. Emanation centered on the darkmantle. The aura lasts for as long as it maintains Concentration, up to 10 minutes. Darkvision cannot see through the darkness, and no light can illuminate the area.

gm.title: Suffocation hazard
lines: A creature suffocating under the darkmantle gains 1 level of Exhaustion at the end of each of its turns. Once it can breathe again, remove the levels it gained from suffocation.

gm.title: Description
lines: This death giant inscribes its magic on a fallen giant’s skull. With the skull in hand, it can give its staff a spectral blade or wrap itself in a shroud of souls.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Death Rune. The giant can use Reaping Scythe and Shroud of Souls while holding or wearing the skull marked with this rune. The skull has AC 18, 35 HP, and immunity to necrotic, poison and psychic damage. It returns to full HP at the end of every turn. It crumbles to dust if it reaches 0 HP or the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can mark another skull it possesses when it finishes a short or long rest.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Soul Burst attacks. If the giant has its death rune, it can make three Reaping Scythe attacks instead.
Soul Burst. Melee or ranged spell attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d10 + 6) necrotic damage. If the target is frightened, the giant gains temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt.
Reaping Scythe (Requires Death Rune). Melee spell attack, +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one creature. A hit deals 38 (7d10) necrotic damage. The creature cannot regain hit points until the end of its next turn and dies if this attack reduces it to 0 HP.
Spellcasting. The giant casts one spell from this list using Intelligence. At will, Detect Magic and Mage Armor. Three times per day each, Speak with Dead and Tenser’s Floating Disk. Mage Armor raises AC to 15.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Frightening Teleport (Recharge 4–6). Magically teleport the giant and its worn or carried equipment up to 40 ft. to an unoccupied space it can see. Each creature within 10 ft. of the space the giant left must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom save or become frightened until the end of that creature’s next turn.
Shroud of Souls (Requires Death Rune). The giant surrounds itself with a torrent of souls. A creature starting its turn within 5 ft. of the shrouded giant must pass a DC 19 Wisdom save or have disadvantage on saving throws until the end of its next turn. The shroud ends after 1 minute or sooner if the giant dies, uses Shroud of Souls again, or loses its death rune to destruction.

lines:

gm.title: Description
lines: This undead beholder surrounds its floating skull with spectral eyes and uses its former victims as guards.

gm.title: Defenses and senses
lines: Natural armor. Perception +12, passive Perception 22. Immune to poison damage and to Charmed, Exhaustion, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned and Prone. Darkvision 120 ft. Deep Speech and Undercommon.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink or sleep.
Negative Energy Cone. At the start of its turn, choose whether its central eye projects an invisible magical 150-ft. cone and which direction it faces. Creatures in the cone cannot regain HP. A humanoid that dies there keeps its initiative and rises at the start of its next turn as a Zombie under the tyrant’s command if its body has not been entirely destroyed.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (4d6) piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Roll three distinct d10 results, rerolling duplicates. Shoot the matching rays at one to three targets it can see within 120 ft.

gm.title: Eye rays
lines:
1. Charm Ray. Wisdom DC 17 or Charmed by the eye tyrant for 1 hour. If it harms the target, the charm ends.
2. Paralyzing Ray. Constitution DC 17 or Paralyzed for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the condition on a success.
3. Fear Ray. Wisdom DC 17 or Frightened for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the condition on a success.
4. Slowing Ray. Dexterity DC 17 or speed is halved for 1 minute. While slowed, the target cannot take reactions and can take only one of an action and a bonus action on its turn. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on a success.
5. Enervation Ray. Constitution DC 17. Failure deals 36 (8d8) necrotic damage. Success halves it.
6. Telekinetic Ray. A creature makes a DC 17 Strength save. On failure, move it up to 30 ft. in any direction. It is Restrained until the start of the eye tyrant’s next turn or until the eye tyrant becomes Incapacitated. An object weighing 300 lb. or less, neither worn nor carried, can move up to 30 ft. in any direction without a save. The ray can also work a simple tool or open a door or container.
7. Sleep Ray. Wisdom DC 17 or Unconscious for 1 minute. Damage or another creature spending an action to wake the target ends the sleep. Constructs and Undead are unaffected.
8. Petrification Ray. Dexterity DC 17 or Restrained and beginning to turn to stone. Repeat the save at the end of the target’s next turn. Success ends the effect. Failure leaves the target Petrified until Greater Restoration or other magic frees it.
9. Disintegration Ray. A creature makes a DC 17 Dexterity save or takes 45 (10d8) force damage. If that damage leaves it at 0 HP, its body turns to fine gray dust. A Large or smaller nonmagical object or creation of magical force is destroyed without a save. For a Huge or larger object or creation of magical force, destroy one 10-ft. cube of it.
10. Death Ray. Dexterity DC 17 or take 55 (10d10) necrotic damage. If this leaves the target at 0 HP, it dies.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Three legendary actions. Spend one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Regain spent actions at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Eye Ray (1 action). Use one randomly rolled eye ray.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
In its lair, the death tyrant is CR 15 (13,000 XP). Act on initiative count 20, losing ties. No lair action while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before the first turn if surprised.
Spectral Obstruction. Choose a 50-ft. cube within 120 ft. Spectral eyes and tentacles make it Lightly Obscured and Difficult Terrain for creatures other than the tyrant until initiative count 20 next round.
Spectral Grasp. Walls sprout spectral limbs until initiative count 20 on the round after next. A hostile creature, even on the Ethereal Plane, that starts its turn within 10 ft. of a wall makes a DC 17 Dexterity save or becomes Grappled. Escape with a DC 17 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
Spectral Eye. An eye appears in the air at a point within 50 ft. and fires one random eye ray at a target the tyrant chooses. The ray comes from an ethereal source. The eye then disappears.
Use all three effects before repeating one, and never repeat on consecutive rounds.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Creatures within 1 mile of the lair sometimes feel watched. Whenever a creature that knows about the tyrant and is hostile to it finishes a Long Rest within 1 mile, roll a d20 for that creature. On a 10 or lower it is subjected to one random eye ray.
After the tyrant dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: In Charm Ray, the book says “beholder” once in the death tyrant’s rules. Treat that reference as the death tyrant.

gm.title: Description
lines: A beholder can pursue its designs after death as an immense floating skull orbited by ten magical eyes.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, Exhaustion, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Legendary Resistance (3/day, 4/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Eye Rays three times.
Bite. Melee attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Choose a visible target within 120 ft. and roll 1d10 for its magical ray. Reroll a ray the death tyrant has already used during this turn. All saves below are DC 17.
1. Charm Ray. Wisdom save. Failure deals 13 (3d8) psychic damage and leaves the target Charmed for 1 hour or until it takes damage. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
2. Paralyzing Ray. Constitution save. Failure leaves the target Paralyzed. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on success. It automatically succeeds after 1 minute.
3. Fear Ray. Wisdom save. Failure deals 10 (3d6) psychic damage and leaves the target Frightened until the end of its next turn. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
4. Slowing Ray. Constitution save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. Until the end of its next turn, the target has half Speed, cannot take Reactions, and has to choose between taking an action and taking a Bonus Action on its turn. Success halves the damage and avoids the other effects.
5. Enervation Ray. Constitution save. Failure deals 16 (3d10) poison damage and leaves the target Poisoned until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned this way, it cannot regain HP. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
6. Telekinetic Ray. Strength save. A Gargantuan target succeeds automatically. On failure the death tyrant moves the target up to 30 ft. in any direction and Restrains it until the start of the death tyrant’s next turn or until the death tyrant is Incapacitated. This ray can also manipulate objects precisely, for example to open a door or operate a tool.
7. Sleep Ray. Wisdom save. Constructs and Undead succeed automatically. On failure the target is Unconscious for 1 minute. Damage ends the effect. A creature within 5 ft. can also use an action to wake the target.
8. Petrification Ray. Constitution save. Failure leaves the target Restrained. If it is still Restrained at the end of its next turn, it repeats the save. Success ends the effect. Failure changes Restrained to Petrified.
9. Disintegration Ray. Dexterity save. Failure deals 36 (8d8) force damage and disintegrates a 10-ft. cube of a targeted nonmagical object or magical force creation. Success halves the damage. Either way, a creature reduced to 0 HP by the ray turns to dust.
10. Death Ray. Dexterity save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) necrotic damage and success halves it. A creature reduced to 0 HP by the ray dies.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Negative Energy Cone. An imperceptible magical wave from its central eye covers a 150-ft. Cone. Creatures in the cone cannot regain HP until its next turn starts. Any intact Humanoid corpse in the cone immediately rises as its controlled Zombie and acts right after it on the same initiative count.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Chomp. Make two Bite attacks.
Glare. Use Eye Rays.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Negative Energy Suffusion. Whenever a spell restores a creature’s HP within 1 mile of the lair, subtract 1d10 from the amount healed.
Scopophobia. Creatures within 1 mile feel watched. A creature other than the death tyrant or its allies that finishes a Short Rest within that area makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On failure the rest grants no benefit.
Both effects end immediately if the death tyrant dies or its lair moves.

lines: A warlock who broke a pact and rose from the dead to finish its patron’s work. A powerful necromancer can bind a deathlock as well.

gm.title: Languages
lines: The languages it knew in life.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Turn Resistance. The Deathlock has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.

gm.title: Undead nature
lines: The Deathlock does not need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
The Deathlock uses Charisma (save DC 13) for its innate spells. It needs no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Mage Armor.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
A 5th-level warlock spellcaster using Charisma (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). It regains spent slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips (at will). Chill Touch, Eldritch Blast, Mage Hand.
1st through 3rd level (two 3rd-level slots). Arms of Hadar, Dispel Magic, Hold Person, Hunger of Hadar, Invisibility, Spider Climb.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Deathly Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) necrotic damage.

gm.title: Patron-specific spells
lines:
The sidebar offers patron lists for replacing some or all of the leveled warlock spells. Keep the base spell slots and cantrips.
Archfey patron. Blink, Faerie Fire, Hunger of Hadar, Hypnotic Pattern, Phantasmal Force, Sleep.
Fiend patron. Blindness/Deafness, Burning Hands, Command, Fireball, Hellish Rebuke, Scorching Ray.
Great Old One patron. Armor of Agathys, Detect Thoughts, Dissonant Whispers, Hunger of Hadar, Tasha's Hideous Laughter, Phantasmal Force.

gm.title: Description
lines: A powerful Deathlock with enough freedom to plan its own tactics. It recruits servants and builds conspiracies to carry out its patron’s orders.

gm.title: Languages
lines: The languages it knew in life.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Turn Resistance. The Deathlock has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.

gm.title: Undead nature
lines: The Deathlock does not need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
The Deathlock uses Charisma (save DC 14) for its innate spells. It needs no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Mage Armor.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
A 10th-level warlock spellcaster using Charisma (save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). It regains spent slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips (at will). Chill Touch, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Poison Spray.
1st through 5th level (two 5th-level slots). Arms of Hadar, Blight, Counterspell, Crown of Madness, Darkness, Dimension Door, Dispel Magic, Fly, Hold Monster, Invisibility.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Deathly Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) necrotic damage.
Grave Bolts. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one or two targets. A hit deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. A target of Large size or smaller must pass a DC 16 Strength save or be restrained by shadowy tendrils for 1 minute. A restrained target can use its action to repeat the save and end the effect on a success.

gm.title: Patron-specific spells
lines:
The sidebar offers patron lists for replacing some or all of the leveled warlock spells. Keep the base spell slots and cantrips.
Archfey patron. Blink, Dominate Beast, Dominate Person, Faerie Fire, Greater Invisibility, Hunger of Hadar, Hypnotic Pattern, Phantasmal Force, Seeming, Sleep.
Fiend patron. Blindness/Deafness, Burning Hands, Command, Fire Shield, Fireball, Flame Strike, Hellish Rebuke, Scorching Ray, Stinking Cloud, Wall of Fire.
Great Old One patron. Clairvoyance, Detect Thoughts, Dissonant Whispers, Dominate Person, Evard's Black Tentacles, Hunger of Hadar, Phantasmal Force, Sending, Tasha's Hideous Laughter, Telekinesis.
