gm.title: Description
lines: A winged jailer of the Veil of Sleep watches its prey unseen before attacking with four claws.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC 15 (+2 Dex, +3 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 13. Base attack +8, grapple +11. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +8, Ref +8, Will +9.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +11 melee (1d4+3). Full attack. Four claws +11 melee (1d4+3 each).
Lullaby (Su). As a standard action, opponents within 20 ft. must make a DC 14 Will save. Failure fatigues them for 1d4 rounds or as long as the dream spawn keeps speaking within 20 ft. of them. Maintaining the lullaby is a free action. This is a sonic, mind-affecting compulsion.
Memory Drain (Su, 1/day). A successful touch attack deals 1d4 Intelligence damage. Until the victim recovers all of those points, the dream spawn can use Alternate Form to impersonate any creature from the victim's memory.
Alternate Form (Su). Use polymorph on itself as a standard action at caster level 8. The form can last indefinitely. Returning to its own shape is a free action.
Invisibility (Sp). As a standard action, become invisible as the spell at caster level 8. It can stay invisible indefinitely until the effect ends, such as by attacking.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 15/magic. Darkvision 60 ft. It does not need to eat, drink, or breathe. Detect Thoughts (Su). In an inhabited dreamscape, it knows a creature's surface thoughts as though it had studied them for three rounds with detect thoughts, caster level 8, Will DC 15. Fear Eater (Ex). Immune to Fear, Horror, and Madness. A spell targeting it that would normally cause one of those effects heals 1 HP per spell level. When one of its actions makes a dreamer fail a Fear, Horror, or Madness save, it heals 2 HP for a minor outcome, 4 HP for a moderate outcome, or 8 HP for a major outcome.

gm.title: Dream defeat
lines: A dreamer killed by this dream spawn takes a DC 17 Ravenloft Madness save on waking (Will). For consequences and recovery, use the Ravenloft Player’s Handbook, chapter 3. A spawn that wins often returns to terrorize that dreamer again.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +13, Disguise +15, Hide +10, Intimidate +12, Listen +10, Move Silently +10, Sense Motive +12, Spot +10. Alertness (bonus), Flyby Attack, Improved Initiative, Skill Focus (Disguise). Speaks Oneiros and the languages of its current prey.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land or underground (dreams). Solitary. No treasure by default. Always lawful evil. Advances at 9–16 HD (Medium) or 17–24 HD (Large). An ennui sometimes carries a dreamslayer weapon. While dreaming, add +3 to that weapon's existing enhancement bonus, to a maximum of +5. Outside of dreams, use the weapon's normal enhancement bonus.

gm.title: Description
lines: This fire elemental hurls flame between short teleports and sets creatures alight by passing through them.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons. Immune to fire and poison damage and to Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, and Unconscious. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10. Speaks Deep Speech.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fire Form. Pass through an opening as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing. A creature that touches the flame or hits it in melee from within 5 ft. takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. The flame can enter and stop in a hostile creature’s space. The first time it enters a creature’s space on a turn, the creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage and ignites. The burning creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until someone uses an action to extinguish it.
Illumination. Shed bright light out to 30 ft. and dim light for 30 ft. more.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Hurl Flame attacks. Before or after each attack, the flame can teleport up to 10 ft. to a space it sees, even if occupied.
Hurl Flame. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, 120-ft. range, one target. Hit 10 (3d6) fire damage.
Touch. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) fire damage. A creature or flammable object ignites and takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until a creature uses an action to extinguish it.

gm.title: Description
lines: An iron lion created to guard Zybilna’s garden alongside Wrath, the iron hart. Envy demands that intruders kneel before it.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Trampling Charge. If Envy moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hits it with Bite on the same turn, that creature must pass a DC 16 Strength save or fall prone. If the target is prone, Envy can make one Claws attack against it as a bonus action.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 18 (2d12 + 5) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 16 (2d10 + 5) slashing damage.
Petrifying Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure, it begins turning to stone and is restrained. It repeats the save at the end of its next turn. Success ends the effect. Failure leaves it petrified until Greater Restoration or other magic frees it.

gm.title: Palace guardian
lines: Envy uses the 2014 Gorgon as its base, with speech and the Bite and Claws attacks shown here. Zybilna’s magic prevents the two guardians from harming one another. Envy orders disrespectful visitors to leave and attacks those who refuse.

gm.title: Crown of needles
lines: Placing the silver crown on Envy banishes it and the crown to its demiplane until Zybilna recalls them. Wrath turns the silver crown to gold. Gold on Envy unlocks lion-marked palace doors even if Envy is dead. To borrow the gold crown, offer a lei of palace flowers. It takes 1 hour for one person to make, divided among contributors. Each contributor may make a DC 15 Intelligence (Nature) check. A success earns the crown temporarily. A total of 25 or higher earns it whenever requested.

lines:
While holding the staff, add +2 to spell attack rolls. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 per dawn. If the last charge is spent, the staff becomes mundane on a roll of 1 on a d20.
One action, using Eoghan’s spell save DC. Animal Friendship (1), Awaken (5), Barkskin (2), Locate Animals or Plants (2), Speak with Animals (1), Speak with Plants (3), or Wall of Thorns (6). Pass without Trace costs no charge.

gm.title: Encounter notes
lines: Three treants defend Eoghan if he is attacked. His Resurrection ritual requires a living humanoid sacrifice whose level or CR equals or exceeds the deceased’s, a diamond or delerium substitute, and a personal offering. If he uses delerium in place of the diamond, the revived creature gains a random Drakkenheim Madness.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Description
lines: An armored, winged devil fights with a withering sword and uses a magic rope to bind its enemies from a distance.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Diabolical Restoration. Death outside the Nine Hells makes the devil vanish in sulfurous smoke. It immediately gains a new body at full HP somewhere in the Nine Hells.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
Magic Rope. The erinyes can use Entangling Rope while bearing its magic rope. The rope has AC 20, 90 HP, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. It crumbles to dust at 0 HP, after spending at least 1 hour at least 5 ft. from the erinyes, or when the erinyes dies. The erinyes can restore the rope in full at the end of a Short or Long Rest if it is damaged or destroyed.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Withering Sword attacks. The erinyes can also use Entangling Rope.
Withering Sword. Melee attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) necrotic damage.
Entangling Rope (requires Magic Rope). Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. It makes a DC 16 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 14 (4d6) force damage and is Restrained until the rope is destroyed, the erinyes releases it as a Bonus Action, or the erinyes uses Entangling Rope again.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Parry. When a melee attack roll hits the erinyes while it is holding a weapon, it can add 4 to its AC against that attack. This can turn the hit into a miss.

gm.title: Description
lines: An organic warship grown by a Reigar, usually resembling a vast jellyfish or cephalopod. Without its creator, its actions are driven by self-preservation.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, petrified, prone.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Bioluminescence. With at least 1 HP, the esthetic lights the area within 30 ft. brightly and the next 30 ft. dimly. Its compartments have dim light.
Spelljamming. The esthetic has the properties of a Spelljamming Helm. Its Reigar creator is the only creature that can attune to it.
Unusual Nature. The esthetic needs no air, food, or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (3d6 + 7) force damage. A creature hit is grappled (escape DC 17) and takes 18 (4d8) acid damage at the start of each of its turns while held. The esthetic has 1d4 × 2 tentacles. Each can grapple one target and cannot attack a different target until it releases the creature.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Jammerscream (recharge 6). Choose one spelljamming ship within 300 ft. If it has several helms, randomly select one. Its helm’s magic shuts down for 2d10 days unless a creature attuned to it opts to make a DC 17 Charisma save. On a failed save, that creature takes 42 (12d6) psychic damage and the shutdown lasts 2d10 hours. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and the shutdown lasts 2d10 minutes.

gm.title: Passengers and creator
lines: There is room for the Reigar and up to six Medium passengers. The Reigar can open or close the hatch by touching it. The esthetic can live indefinitely on the Astral Plane while its creator lives. If its creator dies, the esthetic sickens and dies after 1d12 days.

lines: Saves Dex +6, Con +5. Skills Acrobatics +6, Perception +4, Stealth +8. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 14. Common.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Spider Climb. Traverse difficult surfaces, including ceilings upside down, without making an ability check.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Sting attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature is Grappled (escape DC 14) and takes 2 (1d4) poison damage at the start of each of Excess’s turns. Excess cannot bite anyone else before this grapple ends.
Sting. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage. On a failed DC 13 Constitution save, the target is Poisoned for 1 minute and can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.
Swallow. Use Bite on a Medium or smaller creature grappled by Excess or from which Excess is hidden. On a hit, swallow the creature. It is no longer Grappled, but is Blinded and Restrained and has total cover from attacks and other effects outside Excess. At the start of each of Excess’s turns, it takes 10 (3d6) acid damage. Excess can hold one swallowed creature. If Excess dies, the creature is no longer Restrained and can spend 5 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting Prone.

lines: Cunning Action. Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

lines:
Abominations. Once per encounter for each party action, after an enemy finishes its turn. The party can use the actions in any order, one per round. The creature performing the action must be present and must not be Incapacitated.
Action 2, Hypnotize. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone from Excess must make a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is Charmed by Excess and its speed is 0 until the start of Excess’s next turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Guillotine Blade. Melee or ranged weapon attack +15, reach 10 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target, 30 (6d6 + 9) slashing plus 14 (4d6) necrotic. On a failed DC 21 Constitution save, reduce the target's maximum HP by the necrotic damage taken until it finishes a long rest. A target whose maximum HP becomes 0 dies. The blade returns immediately after a ranged attack.
Necrotic Vents (recharge 5–6). Each creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 21 Constitution save, taking 45 (10d8) necrotic damage on failure or half on success. A creature that fails by 5 or more gains one level of Contamination.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round. Use one option after another creature's turn and recover spent actions at the start of this creature's turn.
Lumber Forward (2 actions). Move up to half speed.
Attack (2 actions). Make a melee or ranged Guillotine Blade attack.
Summon Shadows (3 actions). Up to six visible humanoid corpses within 60 ft. that died violently each produce a shadow in their space or the nearest empty one. They obey the Executioner and act after it on the same initiative count. They disappear after 1 minute or if the Executioner is destroyed, and can be destroyed earlier.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Description
lines: With mouth and eye shut, this ambusher resembles a twelve-foot asteroid. It opens its eye when it senses vibrations. Coins, metal weapons, gems, and magic items can remain in the gullet after a meal.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Darkvision 120 ft., blindsight 120 ft. while the eye monger's eye is closed.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Antimagic Gullet. The gullet suppresses magic, including spells and magic items. Magic from artifacts or deities is exempt. Slots or item charges spent inside on suppressed magic are wasted. Suppression counts against an effect’s duration. Outside magic cannot affect creatures or objects inside unless it comes from an artifact or deity.
False Appearance. If it starts combat motionless with both mouth and eye closed, it has advantage on initiative. A creature that has never seen it move or act needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize it as animate.
Unusual Nature. The eye monger needs no air.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit must pass a DC 18 Dexterity save or be swallowed into the antimagic gullet. The eye monger can hold one swallowed creature at a time.
A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained. It has total cover from attacks and other effects originating outside the eye monger. It takes 35 (10d6) acid damage at the start of each of its own turns.
If a creature in the gullet deals at least 25 damage to the eye monger in one turn, the monster regurgitates it. The creature lands prone within 10 ft. If the eye monger dies, the swallowed creature is freed from restraint and can spend 10 ft. of movement to exit prone.

gm.title: Printing note

lines: A beholder’s dreams of a dragon rival can give rise to this limbless flying aberration. A large eye in its mouth projects antimagic, and the eyestalks in its wings fire rays.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Unusual Nature. The eyedrake needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Antimagic Breath (Recharge 6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Constitution save. Failure deals 39 (6d12) force damage. Success halves the damage. Every spell of 3rd level or lower ends on creatures or objects of the eyedrake’s choice in the cone.
Eye Rays. Roll three different rays at random, rerolling duplicates. For each ray, choose one creature the eyedrake can see within 60 ft.
1. Freezing Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, take 17 (5d6) cold damage and halve speed until the end of the target’s next turn. Success halves the damage without reducing speed.
2. Debilitating Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, take 7 (2d6) thunder damage and become incapacitated until the end of the target’s next turn.
3. Repulsion Ray. DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, take 14 (4d6) force damage and be pushed up to 60 ft. away from the eyedrake.
4. Fire Ray. DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, take 21 (6d6) fire damage. Success halves the damage.
5. Paralyzing Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, become paralyzed for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
6. Death Ray. DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, take 28 (8d6) necrotic damage. Success halves the damage. The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 hit points.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A gigantic burrowing stalk tipped with a single red eye.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Con +11, Wis +4. Senses: blindsight 30 ft., tremorsense 60 ft.. No languages. Passive Perception 9.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Tunneler. Burrowing through solid rock costs twice as much movement, and leaves a tunnel 10 ft. wide.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Bite once and use Eradication Gaze when available.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +14, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) piercing. A Large or smaller creature must pass a DC 19 Dexterity save or be swallowed. Inside, it is Blinded and Restrained and has Total Cover against attacks and effects from outside. At the start of each eyestalk turn it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage. When one creature inside deals at least 30 damage on a turn, the eyestalk must pass a DC 21 Constitution save at that turn's end or vomit all swallowed creatures out Prone within 10 ft. If the eyestalk dies, swallowed creatures are no longer Restrained by it and can spend 20 ft. of movement to exit Prone.
Eradication Gaze (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 150-ft. cone makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) necrotic damage. A creature reduced to 0 HP by that damage turns into fine violet dust.

gm.title: Description
lines: A green, blue, indigo, or violet faerie dragon. These older butterfly-winged dragons build on the magic they learned in earlier colors.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A cat-sized dragon with butterfly wings. Older forms range from green through blue and indigo to violet.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Arcana +4, Perception +3, Stealth +7. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 13. Draconic and Sylvan.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Superior Invisibility. As a bonus action, the dragon can turn itself and its worn or carried gear Invisible. It maintains Concentration as it would on a spell. The effect ends when its concentration ends.
Limited Telepathy. The dragon can communicate magically with any other faerie dragon within 60 ft.
Magic Resistance. The dragon has advantage on saves against spells and other magic.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Innate Spellcasting. Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 13). The dragon needs no material components. Each color adds its spells to those of all younger colors.
Red (5 years or less), 1/day each. Dancing Lights, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
Orange (6–10 years), 1/day. Color Spray.
Yellow (11–20 years), 1/day. Mirror Image.
Green (21–30 years), 1/day. Suggestion.
Blue (31–40 years), 1/day. Major Image.
Indigo (41–50 years), 1/day. Hallucinatory Terrain.
Violet (51 years or more), 1/day. Polymorph.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 1 piercing damage.
Euphoria Breath (Recharge 5–6). Exhale a puff of gas at one creature within 5 ft. It must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or lose its reactions for 1 minute. At the start of each affected turn, roll 1d6. On 1–4, it takes no action or bonus action and spends all its movement moving in a random direction. On 5–6, it stays put and can only repeat the DC 11 Wisdom save, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Variant rules
lines: Superior Invisibility is a bonus action and requires Concentration. Worn and carried gear also becomes Invisible.

Euphoria Breath (Recharge 5–6) targets one creature within 5 ft. It must pass a DC 11 Wisdom save or lose reactions for 1 minute. At each turn start roll a d6. On 1–4 it takes no action or bonus action and uses all its movement in a random direction. On 5–6 it stays still and can only repeat the save to end the effect.

gm.title: Faerie Dragon Color and Age
lines: Age by color. Red up to 5 years, orange 6–10, yellow 11–20, green 21–30, blue 31–40, indigo 41–50, and violet 51 or more.

Each spell is usable once per day. Red gains Dancing Lights, Mage Hand and Minor Illusion. Orange adds Color Spray and yellow adds Mirror Image. Green adds Suggestion, blue Major Image, indigo Hallucinatory Terrain and violet Polymorph. Each color keeps all spells of younger colors.
Red through yellow are CR 1. Green through violet are CR 2. Innate spell save DC 13.

gm.title: Description
lines: Far traders sail the Astral Sea to sell luxury goods and magic-infused stones. Their hidden home port is the black-rock city of Far Spire.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Studded leather. Perception 15, Stealth 12. Vulnerable to radiant damage and resistant to necrotic damage. Darkvision 120 ft. Speaks all languages.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +1, Dex +2, Con +4, Int +3, Wis +5, Cha +6

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Astral Seafarer. Proficient with airships and waterborne vessels. Add its proficiency bonus to checks to control such a vessel and grant advantage on saves made aboard.
Ethereal Sight. See 60 ft. across the boundary between the Material and Ethereal Planes from either side.
Far Traveler. Advantage on saves against environmental dangers such as Void terrain and infernal gases.
Phrenic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical and add 2d4 psychic damage on a hit, included below.
Regeneration. Regain 2 HP at the start of each turn. Fire or radiant damage disables this trait at the start of its next turn. The trader dies only if it starts a turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Trader’s Eye. Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks to spot defective or counterfeit goods and on Wisdom (Insight) checks to catch someone trying to sell those goods.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar or Psychic Bolt attacks. The trader can replace one with Spellcasting.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage plus 5 (2d4) psychic damage.
Psychic Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) psychic damage.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: Charisma, save DC 14. At will: Message, Minor Illusion. Three times per day each: Disguise Self, Suggestion.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Etherealness. Switch between the Material and Ethereal Planes. The trader remains visible from the other plane, but cannot affect or be affected by anything there.
Trader’s Jargon. One creature the trader can see within 30 ft. makes a DC 14 Charisma save. On a failure, it is vulnerable to psychic damage until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: A Carceri fiend coated in sticky tar. Farastus are cruel trackers sometimes charged with hunting down escaped prisoners.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A lanky climbing fiend with long claws, a biting maw, and a sticky hide.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Boundless Movement. Ignore difficult terrain and any magical reduction in speed. The farastu can spend 5 ft. of movement to end the grappled condition on itself automatically.
Magic Resistance. The farastu has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Spider Climb. Traverse hard-to-climb surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks and one Bite attack.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) slashing damage. A Large or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 15, with disadvantage on the escape check). The farastu can hold one creature in each claw.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Roll with advantage against a creature the farastu is grappling. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing plus 24 (7d6) acid damage.
Summon Demodand (1/day). There is a 40 percent chance another farastu appears in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. It fights as an ally and cannot summon other demodands. It stays up to 1 minute and disappears sooner if either farastu dies or the summoner dismisses it as an action.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:

Charisma, no material components. At will: Invisibility (self only). 1/day each: Dispel Magic and Fog Cloud.

gm.title: Demodands
lines: Carceri’s bureaucratic Kelubar Demodands rank above farastus and often send them to do their fighting. A demodand that dies outside Carceri reforms there after 2d20 days.

lines:

gm.title: Description
lines: A silver-patterned celestial cat that forms a close bond with one creature. Azorius officials use these bonds to help locate escaped prisoners.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Understands Celestial and Common but can't speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Bonding. The felidar can form a magical bond with a creature it can see immediately after observing it for at least 1 hour within 30 ft. The bond ends if that creature dies or the felidar bonds with another creature. The partners can speak telepathically within 100 ft. On the same plane the felidar can sense how far away its partner is and in which direction. Either partner can take an action to see and hear through the other's senses until the start of its next turn. While doing so, it loses its own sight and hearing.
Keen Hearing and Sight. The felidar makes Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or sight with advantage.
Pounce. After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hitting it with Claws on the same turn, the victim must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone. If the victim is prone, the felidar can make a Claws attack against it as a bonus action.

gm.title: Description
lines: At the full moon, these golden marsh hounds track someone who has committed a deed that calls for a powers check.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Temperate marsh. Pair or pack of 5–8. Always chaotic good. No treasure. Advancement 6–10 HD (Large). No level adjustment listed.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC +2 Dex and +6 natural, touch 12, flat-footed 16. Base attack +4, grapple +8. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +6, Ref +6, Will +4.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Listen +7, Move Silently +9, Spot +7, Survival +7. Endurance, Track.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Damage reduction 5/—, scent, spell resistance 14. Magic Immunity (Ex). Immune to Sun domain spells. Spells cast by priests of deities of the moon, moors, or revenge cannot harm it.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Bite +8 melee (1d8 + 4).
Trip (Ex). After a bite hits, make a trip check at +4 as a free action. No touch attack or attack of opportunity, and the target cannot counter-trip on a failure.
Bay (Su). At the start of the hunt its howl carries one mile. The quarry must immediately attempt a DC 13 Fear save if it hears the bay.

gm.title: The hunt
lines: A deed requiring a powers check in a swamp or moor draws at least two hounds on the next full moon. They track the quarry unerringly, fight anyone who interferes, and vanish at dawn. They return on the three nights of a full moon while the quarry survives and the curse remains. A slain hound dissolves into luminous vapor. Recurrence (Su). Killing a fenhound makes the killer the target of a pack at each full moon. Atonement ends the pursuit.

gm.title: Ravenloft Fear
lines: When using the Ravenloft Fear rules, roll a Will save. Apply modifiers to saves against fear. Failure by 1–5 makes the target shaken, 6–10 frightened, and 11–15 panicked. Failure by 16 or more makes it panicked and calls for an immediate Horror save at the Fear DC minus 5. Fear lasts 5d6 rounds. A second failure escalates shaken to frightened or frightened to panicked. Creatures without Intelligence scores are immune. See Ravenloft Player’s Handbook, pp. 77–79.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Deflecting Chain. When an attack hits, add 3 to AC against it, which can turn the hit into a miss.

lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: After a thousand years or more in Ysgard, some fensirs grow to about 25 feet tall and develop a hunger they cannot satisfy. A devourer can curse nearby creatures as it dies.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Death Curse. If the fensir starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate, each creature within 30 ft. of it when it dies must make a DC 13 Charisma save. A creature that fails is cursed for 24 hours. It gains no benefit from a short or long rest and must make a DC 13 Charisma save at the end of every hour or take 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
Regeneration. The fensir regains 10 HP at the start of its turn if outside sunlight. Taking acid or fire damage suppresses regeneration at the start of its next turn. The fensir dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. If the fensir starts its turn in sunlight, it must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be petrified until it is out of the sunlight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks in any combination of Rend and Boulder.
Rend. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d10 + 5) slashing damage.
Boulder. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d12 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 16 Strength save or fall prone. Roll a d6 after each throw. On a 4 or lower, the fensir runs out of boulders.

gm.title: Traits

Sunlight Hypersensitivity. If the fensir starts its turn in sunlight, it must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be petrified until it is out of the sunlight.

lines:

Magic Stone. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d12 + 2) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
Mud to Stone (Recharge 6). Choose a point the fensir can see within 60 ft. Magical mud fills a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered there. Each creature other than a fensir in the sphere must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity save or take 13 (3d8) bludgeoning damage and become restrained. The creature must roll the save again at the end of its next turn. A success ends the effect, while a failure petrifies it for 24 hours.
Spellcasting. The fensir uses Intelligence to cast Create or Destroy Water, Detect Magic, or Pass without Trace. It can cast each spell once per day.

gm.title: Description
lines: The high priest of Dendar in Omu. A vision of the Black Opal Crown convinced her to plot a coup against Ras Nsi.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Darkvision 120 ft., including in magical darkness.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Death Fangs (2/day). The first time Fenthaza hits with a melee attack on her turn, she can add 16 (3d10) necrotic damage.
Magic Resistance. She has advantage on saves against spells and other magic.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Shapechanger. Change into a Medium snake or back into yuan-ti form. Her equipment and statistics stay the same. She keeps her current form on death.
Multiattack (yuan-ti form only). Make one Constrict and one Scimitar attack.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller target is grappled (escape DC 14) and restrained until the grapple ends. Fenthaza can constrict only one creature at a time.
Scimitar (yuan-ti form only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Invoke Nightmare (short or long rest). Choose a visible creature within 60 ft. It makes a DC 13 Intelligence save. On a failure, it takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage and is frightened of an immobile, indestructible illusion visible only to it. Fenthaza maintains Concentration for up to 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the illusion on a success or taking another 11 (2d10) psychic damage on a failure.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Only in yuan-ti form. Innate magic uses Charisma (save DC 13) and requires no material components. Animal Friendship is at will and works only on snakes. Suggestion is 3/day.
6th-level warlock. Spellcasting uses Charisma (save DC 13, +5 to hit). Recover both 3rd-level slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips: Chill Touch, Eldritch Blast (300 ft., +3 damage per hit), Mage Hand, Message, Poison Spray, Prestidigitation.
3rd-level slots: Arms of Hadar, Darkness, Fear, Hex, Hold Person, Hunger of Hadar, Witch Bolt.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines:
Two type 2 Yuan-ti Malisons guard area 5. Fighting in the hall brings the broodguards from area 6 in 1 round. Fenthaza’s stone urn contains an Air Elemental that obeys her. Anyone else removing the lid releases it to attack. After an alarm, the guards cover Fenthaza while she releases the elemental. She tries to capture intruders alive for area 8 and may send a particularly troublesome captive to the altar in area 6. She carries keys to area 8’s restraints. If the party leaves before the coup, she can send the elemental after them. It returns when the pursuit ends.
If prisoners serve a day of labor without incident, she offers freedom and any of Ras Nsi’s puzzle cubes in exchange for taking him down. The agreement can open the armory and start an uprising. She means to betray the party if she can.

lines: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 111–114 and 117 (Fenthaza, temple roster, and area 5). Uses the Yuan-ti Nightmare Speaker reprinted on p. 239, originally from Volo's Guide to Monsters, p. 205.

gm.title: Description
lines: A hovering tentacled horror that feeds on strong emotions. It avoids confrontation by hiding aboard spelljamming ships and feeding on the nightmares of sleeping crew.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Unusual Nature. The feyr has no need to breathe.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Frightful Bite attack and one Tentacle attack.
Frightful Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Deal 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage on a hit. After the hit, every creature within 10 ft. that can see the feyr must pass a DC 13 Wisdom save or be frightened of it until the end of the feyr's next turn.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. On a hit, the target takes 17 (4d6 + 3) psychic damage and is grappled (escape DC 13). Each of the feyr's two tentacles can hold one creature and cannot attack a different target while holding one.
Invisibility. The feyr turns invisible. An attack or use of Nightmare Fuel ends the effect. It can also end it as a bonus action.
Nightmare Fuel (1/day). Choose an unconscious creature the feyr can see within 10 ft. The target must pass a DC 13 Wisdom save or take 27 (5d10) psychic damage. The feyr gains as many temporary hit points as the damage it actually deals.

gm.title: Description
lines: Rajian artisans animate small statues as guards, assassins, and distractions. The material determines how each construct fights.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: Choose a figurine by its material. A Ceramic Figurine sprays stored liquids. A Crystal Figurine uses patterned lights and reflects light spells. An Ivory Figurine grows to elephant size. An Obsidian Figurine gets underfoot and sprays sharp fragments when hit. A Porcelain Figurine uses enervation rays and grows to tiger size.

gm.title: Control
lines: Once a month, the figurine and its master make opposed Will saves. A win frees the figurine, changes its moral alignment to evil, and sends it after its former master. Figurines understand their creator's language and cannot speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Fire Form. The elemental can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. A creature that touches the elemental or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. In addition, the elemental can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature’s space on a turn, that creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage and catches fire; until someone takes an action to douse the fire, the creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. Illumination. The elemental sheds bright light in a 30- foot radius and dim light in an additional 30 feet. Water Susceptibility. For every 5 feet the elemental moves in water, or for every gallon of water splashed on it, it takes 1 cold damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The elemental makes two touch attacks. Touch. Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) fire damage. If the target is a creature or a flammable object, it ignites. Until a creature takes an action to douse the fire, the target takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

lines:

lines:

On a success it takes half damage. A creature can use an action to make a DC 19 Strength (Athletics) check to free itself or a creature within its reach. Each mass of restraining rock has AC 17, 20 HP, and immunity to fire, poison, and psychic damage.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Antimagic Shell. The snail has advantage on saves against spells, and spell attacks against it have disadvantage. If the snail saves successfully against a spell of 1st level or higher or that spell's attack misses it, its shell releases stored force. Every creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 3 (1d6) force damage per spell level on a failure or half as much on a success.

lines:

lines:

Illumination. The skeleton sheds Bright Light out to 15 ft. and Dim Light for another 15 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Hurl Flame. Ranged attack, +4 to hit, range 60 ft. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) fire damage.

gm.title: Skeleton pantomimes
lines:
Roll 1d6 or choose what the skeleton does when left alone.
1. Takes a meal or old letters to its former master’s tomb.
2. Keeps drilling with other skeletons, even after they hack it to pieces.
3. Repeats an old pastime such as dancing, acting, or reading.
4. Returns to familiar work such as cleaning, cooking, mining, or praying.
5. Reenacts its final moments.
6. Guards the post it held in life.

gm.title: Description
lines: A burning skeleton found where Thordak’s fire scarred the land.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Vulnerable to bludgeoning. Immune to fire damage, poison damage, Exhaustion and Poisoned. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 9. Understands its languages from life but cannot speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, water or sleep.
Heated Weapons. A hit with a metal melee weapon deals an extra 3 (1d6) fire damage. The Shortsword damage already includes it.
Illumination. Bright light extends 10 ft., followed by 10 ft. of dim light.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft. Hit for 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing and 3 (1d6) fire.
Ignite. Choose a Large or smaller creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On failure it is Grappled (escape DC 12) and catches fire. It takes 3 (1d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns, even if the grapple ends. The target or a creature within 5 ft. can spend an action to put out the flames. Another effect that quenches them, such as submersion in water, also stops the damage.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A floating, lavender flumph with eyestalks, trailing tentacles, and an oversized feathered hat.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Skills Arcana +4, History +4, Religion +4. Psychic vulnerability. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12. Understands Undercommon without speaking. Telepathy 60 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Advanced Telepathy. Flapjack perceives the content of any telepathic communication within 60 ft. and cannot be Surprised by telepathic creatures.
Prone Deficiency. When knocked Prone, roll a die. On an odd result, Flapjack lands upside down and becomes Incapacitated. At the end of each of its turns it can make a DC 10 Dexterity save to right itself and end that condition.
Telepathic Shroud. Flapjack is immune to divination spells and effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Tendrils. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of the target's turns, it makes a DC 10 Constitution save. It takes 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure. A success or Lesser Restoration ends the recurring acid damage.
Stench Spray (1/day). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or be coated in a foul liquid for 1d4 hours. A coated creature is Poisoned for the duration. Other creatures are Poisoned while within 5 ft. of it. A creature can remove the stench from itself by bathing in water, alcohol, or vinegar during a short rest.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, Flapjack can cast one of these spells using Intelligence, save DC 12, with no material components.
At will · Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
1/day each · Magic Missile, Unseen Servant.

gm.title: Encounters
lines:
Flapjack pilots Captain Sartell's Moondancer and can teach spellcasters the basics of spelljamming.
The Moondancer's helm lets Flapjack sense telepathic activity aboard nearby ships while piloting. The Lucent Edict's psurlons obscure their presence with Aberrant Mind. Flapjack senses something aboard and shares that with Sartell and close companions.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Rules source: Light of Xaryxis, pp. 13 and 15–16. Base Flumph rules from Monster Manual (2014), p. 135.

gm.title: Description

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: Flask and River Mist quietly hire out in Malar’s Throat and Tiryki Anchorage. They can guide travelers to Firefinger or Dungrunglung. The Zhentarim pay attention to what the two learn about Artus Cimber, and the pair report back unless given a reason to keep quiet.

gm.title: Description
lines: An adamantine skeleton supports the bodies of fallen giants. An elemental core inside the chest powers the construct and keeps it under control.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: lightning, poison, psychic, bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Berserk. Destroying the core makes the colossus berserk until it is destroyed. On each of its turns it attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is close enough to reach and attack, it attacks an object.
Immutable Form. Spells and other effects cannot change its form.
Magic Resistance. The colossus has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Fist attacks.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Roll with advantage while berserk. A hit deals 17 (3d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit is pulled up to 15 ft. toward the colossus and becomes grappled (escape DC 17). It is restrained until this grapple ends. The colossus can hold up to two creatures this way.
Elemental Breath (Recharge 5–6). Choose acid, cold, fire, or lightning. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 40 (9d8) damage of the chosen type on a failure or half as much on a success. When it exhales, creatures inside its chest cavity also take 40 (9d8) force damage.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Large or smaller creature grappled by the colossus. A hit deals 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage and swallows the creature. The chest cavity can hold up to two swallowed creatures. A swallowed creature is restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects outside the colossus, and takes 10 (3d6) force damage at the start of each of the colossus’s turns.

gm.title: Elemental core
lines: The core is a Large object within the chest cavity with AC 16, 140 HP, and immunity to lightning, poison, and psychic damage. It sheds dim light in a 10-ft. radius. Destroying it makes the colossus berserk and prevents further swallowing. The colossus ejects all swallowed creatures, which land prone in spaces within 10 ft. If the colossus dies, swallowed creatures lose the restrained condition and can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Berserk. Whenever the golem starts its turn with 40 hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points. The golem’s creator, if within 60 feet of the berserk golem, can try to calm it by speaking firmly and persuasively. The golem must be able to hear its creator, who must take an action to make a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check. If the check succeeds, the golem ceases being berserk. If it takes damage while still at 40 hit points or fewer, the golem might go berserk again. Aversion of Fire. If the golem takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn. Immutable Form. The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form. Lightning Absorption. Whenever the golem is subjected to lightning damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of hit points equal to the lightning damage dealt. Magic Resistance. The golem has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Magic Weapons. The golem’s weapon attacks are magical.

The fleshcrawler can issue telepathic orders, which the target tries to follow. Once it completes an order, it acts on its own and concentrates on protecting itself until it receives another. It repeats the save whenever damaged and at the end of each day, ending the effect on a success. If the full duration elapses with the target still Charmed, it dies and its body becomes a cocoon. A new fleshcrawler hatches an hour later.

Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.

Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the horror has disadvantage on attacks and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once it succeeds on the save or the effect ends, it is immune to this horror’s screech for 24 hours.

gm.title: Customizing a Horror
lines:
For a customized Flying Horror, choose or roll one primary and one secondary feature on two d4s.
Primary 1. Avoidance. If a successful save would halve damage, take no damage on a success and half as much on a failure.
Primary 2. Damage Resistances. Gain resistance to necrotic and psychic damage.
Primary 3. Innate Spellcasting. Cast Darkness three times per day using Charisma (spell save DC 13), without material components.
Primary 4. Psychic Rebuke. When a melee attack deals damage to the horror, it can use its reaction to deal 3 (1d6) psychic damage to each creature within 5 ft.
Secondary 1. Grasping Tendrils. The horror has four tendrils (AC 12 and 10 HP each). Destroying one deals no damage to the horror. As a bonus action, choose a creature it can see within 10 ft. The target makes a DC 9 Dexterity save or is grappled (escape DC 9). Each tendril can hold only one target at a time.
Secondary 2. Indomitable Mind. Gain immunity to being charmed.
Secondary 3. Keen Senses. Gain advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, hearing, or smell.
Secondary 4. Mind Sight. Magical darkness does not impede the horror’s darkvision.

gm.title: Horrors and Madness
lines: If you use the book’s optional madness rule, track each failed save against a Flying Horror’s Frightening Screech, a Shadow Horror’s claw attack, or a Skittering Horror’s Maddening Presence. After the encounter, each character with any such failures makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. Failure causes short-term madness after one tracked failure, long-term madness after two or three, or indefinite madness after four or more. Consult the Dungeon Master’s Guide for the corresponding madness rules.

lines: A creature within 5 ft. notices the depression in the horse’s forehead. A successful DC 10 Intelligence check identifies it as the former site of a horn. lines: A pact with a power of the Underdark lets this warlock shape darkness into a weapon.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

The object has AC 15 and 30 HP and is immune to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It regains all HP at the end of every turn. It crumbles to dust at 0 HP or when the fomorian dies. gm.title: Actions
lines:

Corrupting Hex (requires Blood Rune). Choose one creature the fomorian can see within 60 ft. On a failed DC 16 Charisma save, it takes 27 (6d8) necrotic damage and is cursed for 24 hours. The curse halves its speed. Before casting a spell, it must pass a DC 16 Intelligence check or the spell fails and is wasted.

lines: Natural armor. Saves Con +16, Wis +10, Cha +13. Athletics +17, Perception +10. Immune to fire and radiant damage. Passive Perception 20. Immune to Charmed, Dazed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified and Stunned. Blindsight 120 ft., truesight 60 ft. Common and Draconic.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Hellfire. Her fire damage ignores resistance.
Ireful Defense (3/day). On a failed save, Forzaantilirys can succeed instead. Attacks against her then have advantage until the end of her next turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +17, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing plus 14 (4d6) fire damage. The target catches fire.
Claw. Melee weapon attack +17, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d6 + 10) slashing damage. Forzaantilirys can move the target up to 15 ft. horizontally.
Scorching Breath (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 90-ft. cone make a DC 24 Dexterity save. Failure deals 70 (20d6) fire damage and destroys mundane metal items the creature wears or carries. Success halves the damage and preserves its gear. The cone stays aflame as difficult terrain until the end of Forzaantilirys’s next turn. A creature takes 14 (4d6) fire damage when it first enters that area on a turn or ends its turn there.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Blazing Rush. Forzaantilirys moves up to half her speed. A creature takes 10 (3d6) fire damage if she enters its space during this move.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Ignite the Insolent. When a creature attacks her from within 120 ft., the attacker makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. It catches fire on a failure.

gm.title: Catching fire
lines: A creature set on fire by Bite or Ignite the Insolent takes 10 (3d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute. The creature or anyone who can reach it can use an action to put out the flames. Ignition on a later turn resets the duration without stacking damage.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Use each once per encounter, in any order after an enemy’s turn, and at most one per round.
Cinderfall. Smoke and cinders fill a 30-ft.-radius area around Forzaantilirys until the end of her next turn. The area is heavily obscured to everyone else. An enemy that needs to breathe and starts its turn inside must pass a DC 21 Constitution save or be Poisoned for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Ashen Armor. Gain 100 temporary hit points. While any of them remain, a creature within 5 ft. that touches her or hits her with an attack takes 14 (4d6) fire damage.
Supernova. Each creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 21 Constitution save. Failure deals 35 (10d6) fire plus 35 (10d6) radiant damage and leaves the creature Blinded until a spell, power, or similar supernatural effect removes the condition. Success halves the damage and avoids the blindness.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn, a Dazed creature can move, take an action, or take a bonus action. It chooses just one. If it becomes Dazed on its turn, its turn ends. Extra actions such as those from Haste and Action Surge still apply. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration and Greater Restoration can end the condition.

gm.title: Description
lines: A water fey who plays enchanted tunes near streams and waterfalls. Its music can disorient intruders or send a wave crashing over them.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 15, Stealth 16. Resists cold damage. Immune to Charmed. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Common, Elvish, and Sylvan.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +1, Dex +6, Con +2, Int +1, Wis +2, Cha +7

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Breathes air and water.
Fey Resilience. The printed trait grants resistance to Charmed and Unconscious. The stat line grants immunity to Charmed.
Magic Resistance. Has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Discordant Chord attacks.
Discordant Chord. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit 17 (4d6 + 3) thunder damage.
Torrential Tune (2/day). Each creature in a 20-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Failure deals 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage and knocks it Prone. Success halves the damage and prevents the fall.
Spellcasting. Uses Charisma (save DC 15) and its instrument as the only material component. At will: Fog Cloud, Prestidigitation. Three times per day each: Charm Monster, Water Breathing. Once per day each: Control Weather, Disguise Self.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Bewildering Harmonics. One visible creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure it is confused through the end of its next turn and cannot take reactions. Roll 1d8 for that turn. On 1–4 it does nothing. On 5–6 it spends all its movement going in a random direction and takes neither an action nor a bonus action. On 7–8 it makes a melee attack against a random creature in reach or does nothing if none is available.
Ventriloquistic Step. Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Cacophonous Note (Recharge 5–6). When a visible creature within 30 ft. succeeds on an attack, check, or save, force it to reroll and use the new result.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saving throws Str +7 and Con +7. Resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from mundane attacks. Immune to poison damage and to Charmed, Dazed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, and Prone. Blindsight 90 ft., passive Perception 11. Speaks Primordial.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Churning Trunk. The cryptic can pass through a Prone creature’s space without provoking opportunity attacks from Prone creatures. The first time in a turn it crosses a Prone enemy’s space, that enemy takes 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks and use Stone Bone Storm.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Stone Bone Storm. Each creature in a 30-ft.-long, 5-ft.-wide line from the cryptic makes a DC 15 Strength save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage and knocks it Prone. Success halves the damage and prevents the fall. Then the cryptic reforms in an unoccupied space within the line.
Shatterstone (recharge 6). Burrow up to half its speed. If within 5 ft. of the surface at the end of this movement, the cryptic can breach it. Each other creature within 20 ft. then makes a DC 15 Dexterity save for half of 36 (8d8) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Stoneshift. Choose one creature or object touching the ground within 30 ft. A failed DC 15 Dexterity save lets the cryptic move it horizontally up to 15 ft. Objects automatically fail.

gm.title: Description
lines: A Fraternity of Order magistrate who exploits loopholes in planar law to manipulate distance and probability.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A Fraternity magistrate in formal attire who manipulates space and probability.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Small or Medium humanoid, any alignment

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Arcane Burst attacks and use Power of Authority or Spellcasting.
Arcane Burst. Melee or ranged spell attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 90 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d12 + 4) force damage.
Power of Authority. Choose one creature within 60 ft. that the law bender can see. It makes a DC 16 Intelligence save. On a failure, it takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage and is incapacitated for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Any creature that succeeds on the save is immune to this law bender's Power of Authority for 24 hours.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: As an action, use Intelligence to cast Dispel Magic, Fly, Mage Armor, Mage Hand, or Prestidigitation. Each is available at will and needs no material components.

gm.title: Reactions

gm.title: Description
lines: The Prince of Deception recruits mortals under false identities. He sends his servants to find the scattered pieces of the staff taken from him during his imprisonment beneath Castle Greyhawk.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Poison. Nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a save, Fraz-Urb’luu can spend one use to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. He has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Undetectable. Divination magic cannot target him. Magical scrying sensors cannot perceive him, and abilities that sense demons or fiends cannot detect him.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Fist attacks, and use Phantasmal Terror.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d6 + 9) force damage.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d8 + 9) force damage.
Phantasmal Terror. Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. On a failed DC 23 Wisdom save, it takes 16 (3d10) psychic damage and is frightened of Fraz-Urb’luu until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 23). No material components are required.
At will. Alter Self, Detect Magic, Dispel Magic, and Phantasmal Force. Alter Self can make him Medium when he uses its appearance option.
3/day each. Mislead, Programmed Illusion, and Seeming.
1/day each. Modify Memory and Project Image.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Fraz-Urb’luu has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He can choose one option immediately after another creature finishes its turn. He loses access to these actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using one.
Tail (1 action). Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) force damage. A Large or smaller creature is also grappled (escape DC 24) and remains restrained for the duration of the grapple. His tail can grapple only one creature at a time.
Terror (2 actions). Use Phantasmal Terror.

gm.title: Lair
lines: Fraz-Urb’luu lairs in the fortress city of Zoragmelok in Hollow’s Heart. In his lair he is CR 24 (62,000 XP).

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, after anyone tied at 20, choose one action while Fraz-Urb’luu is in his lair. He cannot repeat an option in consecutive rounds. He must be able to act and, if surprised, must finish his first turn before using a lair action.
Conjure Walls and Doors. Turn up to five doors in the lair into walls and open an equal number of new doors in walls that had none.
Psychic Anguish. Every creature he can see in the lair makes a DC 23 Wisdom save, taking 33 (6d10) psychic damage on a failure.
Simulacrum. Pick one humanoid in the lair and instantly make a duplicate as with the Simulacrum spell. The duplicate obeys him and is destroyed at the next initiative count 20.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Choose one or more of these effects for the area surrounding the lair.
Beguiling Realm. Within 6 miles, Charisma (Persuasion) and Wisdom (Insight) checks have disadvantage. Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks have advantage.
Nostalgic Pangs. Within 1 mile, sapient creatures often catch brief glimpses of long-dead friends or companions.
Twisted Paths. Within 6 miles, roads and trails bend back on themselves and make navigation difficult.
If Fraz-Urb’luu dies, the effects fade over 1d10 days.

lines: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 129.

gm.title: Description
lines: The demon lord of illusions wears false identities even when dealing with his own cultists. He looks like a long-necked, winged gargoyle in his true form.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical sources.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Fraz-Urb’luu can choose to succeed when he fails a saving throw.
Magic Resistance. He has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. His weapon attacks are magical.
Undetectable. Divination magic cannot target him, magical scrying sensors cannot reveal him, and abilities that sense demons or fiends cannot detect him.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
Charisma (spell save DC 23). No material components.
At will. Alter Self (can become Medium when changing his appearance), Detect Magic, Dispel Magic, Phantasmal Force.
3/day each. Confusion, Dream, Mislead, Programmed Illusion, Seeming.
1/day each. Mirage Arcane, Modify Memory, Project Image.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Fist attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d6 + 9) piercing damage.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Three legendary actions are available. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Spent actions return at the start of this creature’s turn.
Tail (1 action). Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit by the tail is grappled (escape DC 24) and restrained while grappled. The tail can hold only one creature at a time.
Phantasmal Killer (2 actions). Cast Phantasmal Killer without needing concentration.

gm.title: Lair
lines: Zoragmelok is a circular fortress of twisted towers and domes in Hollow’s Heart. Fraz-Urb’luu is CR 24 (62,000 XP) when encountered in his lair.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option. The same option cannot be used two rounds in a row.
Move doors. Replace up to five doors within the lair with wall and open the same number of new doors in previously solid walls.
Simulacrum. Copy one humanoid within the lair as if by Simulacrum. The copy appears instantly, follows Fraz-Urb’luu’s commands, and is destroyed on the next initiative count 20.
Wave of anguish. Each creature he can see within the lair takes 33 (6d10) psychic damage if it fails a DC 23 Wisdom saving throw.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Intelligent creatures within 1 mile of the lair often glimpse dead friends or comrades that disappear almost immediately.
Within 6 miles, warped roads and paths loop back on themselves and make travel difficult.
A humanoid that spends at least 1 hour within 1 mile must pass a DC 23 Wisdom saving throw or gain a flaw from Madness of Fraz-Urb’luu. A successful save grants immunity to this effect for 24 hours.
These effects fade over 1d10 days after Fraz-Urb’luu dies.

gm.title: Madness of Fraz-Urb’luu
lines:
If a creature goes mad in the lair or within Fraz-Urb’luu’s line of sight, roll d100 for a flaw. It lasts until cured.
01–20. The creature hides the truth about its intentions and actions even when honesty would help.
21–40. Hallucinations and episodes of catatonia come and go.
41–60. The creature drifts into elaborate daydreams and has trouble telling them apart from actual memories.
61–80. The creature holds on to a belief even in the face of overwhelming evidence.
81–100. The creature’s perception of reality differs from everyone else’s, leading to violent delusions.

Reckless. At the start of its turn, the dreg can choose to gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls for that turn. Attacks against it then have advantage until the start of its next turn.
Brute. When the dreg hits with a melee weapon, add one die of that weapon's damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, 5-ft. reach or 20/60-ft. range, one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage. Wielding the spear in two hands for a melee attack deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

gm.title: Haze-native creatures
lines:
Printed source. Appendix A, pp. 196–197. These traits leave the creature’s CR as printed. They apply to Haze natives and exclude creatures recruited or summoned by the party.
Fully Contaminated. Immune to contamination and has advantage on saves against contaminated spells.
Haze Adaptation. Can benefit from a long rest in the Haze. It can see twice as far through the Haze and Deep Haze.
Haze Dependence. Gains one Exhaustion level for each 24 hours outside the Haze. It can remove those levels only in the Haze.
Delerium Healing. As an action, touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) HP. That shard cannot heal this way again for 24 hours.

gm.title: Description
lines: This amphibious predator hides in murky pools with only its three-eyed stalk showing. Bullywugs sometimes feed and shelter one as a god.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The froghemoth breathes air and water.
Shock Susceptibility. When it takes lightning damage, its speed is halved and it has disadvantage on Dexterity saves until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Tentacle attacks. The froghemoth can also use Tongue.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage and swallows a Medium or smaller creature. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects from outside the froghemoth, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the froghemoth's turns. Its gullet holds up to two creatures.
If one creature inside deals 20 damage or more to the froghemoth in a single turn, the froghemoth makes a DC 20 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On a failure, it regurgitates every swallowed creature, which falls prone in a space within 10 ft. If the froghemoth dies, the creatures are no longer restrained and can spend 10 ft. of movement to escape its corpse. Each falls prone on exit.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage and grapples a Huge or smaller creature (escape DC 16). The froghemoth has four tentacles. A tentacle that has a creature grappled cannot target another creature.
Tongue. Target one visible Medium or smaller creature within 20 ft. On a failed DC 18 Strength save, pull it to an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the froghemoth.

gm.title: Description
lines: An amphibious swamp predator with four long tentacles. It leaves only its three-eyed stalk above water while waiting for prey.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The froghemoth breathes both air and water.
Shock Susceptibility. After taking lightning damage, it suffers these effects until the end of its next turn. Its speed is halved, its AC and Dexterity saves take a −2 penalty, and it loses reactions and Multiattack. On its turn it must choose between an action and a bonus action.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks. The froghemoth may also use either Tongue or Bite.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. It also grapples a Huge or smaller creature (escape DC 16). Each of the four tentacles can hold one creature and can’t be used on another target while holding it.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage and swallows a Medium or smaller creature. The gullet holds up to two creatures. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects originating outside the froghemoth, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the froghemoth’s turns. If a creature inside deals at least 20 damage in one turn, the froghemoth must pass a DC 20 Constitution save at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which land prone within 10 ft. If the froghemoth dies, the restraint ends and a swallowed creature can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.
Tongue. One visible Medium or smaller creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 18 Strength save. On a failure, pull it to an empty space within 5 ft. of the froghemoth, which can then use Bite against that creature as a bonus action.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: Kubazan, the trickster god, takes the form of a froghemoth. At his shrine in Omu, a DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check spots a froghemoth’s eyestalk in the murky, 6-ft.-deep pool. It attacks if someone disturbs the water or approaches the shrine, leaving the pool to pursue them (p. 97).
