gm.title: Description
lines: A froghemoth hides in pools with only its three-eyed stalk above the water. Bullywugs sometimes feed and guard one as a god.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The froghemoth can breathe air and water.
Shock Susceptibility. After taking lightning damage, halve its speed and apply a −2 penalty to its AC and Dexterity saves until the end of its next turn. For the same duration, it loses reactions and Multiattack and can use only one action or one bonus action on its turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks. The froghemoth can also use Tongue or Bite.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. A Huge or smaller creature is grappled (escape DC 16). The froghemoth has four tentacles, and a tentacle holding a creature is unavailable against other targets.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage and swallows a Medium or smaller creature, subject to the two-creature limit below.
Tongue. Choose one visible Medium or smaller creature within 20 ft. On a failed DC 18 Strength save, pull it into an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the froghemoth. The froghemoth can then Bite that creature as a bonus action.

gm.title: Swallowing mechanics
lines: The froghemoth holds up to two creatures. Each swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects outside the froghemoth, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the froghemoth's turns. If a creature inside deals at least 20 damage to the froghemoth in one turn, the froghemoth must pass a DC 20 Constitution save at that turn's end or regurgitate all swallowed creatures. They fall prone within 10 ft. If the froghemoth dies, the swallowed creatures are no longer restrained and can spend 10 ft. of movement to exit prone.

gm.title: Description
lines: Frost rune magic lets these giants turn ice into armor or send whole packs of wolves after an intruder.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Frost Rune. The giant must hold or wear the rune-bearing object to use Ice Wolves or Ice Armor. The object has AC 16 and 40 HP and is immune to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It regains all HP at the end of every turn. It crumbles to dust at 0 HP or when the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe one on an object in its possession when it finishes a short or long rest.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The giant can turn a failed saving throw into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Greataxe and Freezing Ray.
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) cold damage.
Freezing Ray. Ranged spell attack, +10 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (3d8 + 4) cold damage, and the target makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure, it is restrained until the end of its next turn. On a success, its speed drops by 10 ft. until the end of its next turn.
Ice Wolves (requires Frost Rune). Magically summon 1d4 ice wolves in unoccupied spaces the giant can see within 30 ft. Use the Winter Wolf stat block and change their creature type to Elemental. They obey the giant and act immediately after it on the same initiative count. Each gains +6 to attack and damage rolls within 30 ft. of the giant. They vanish after 1 minute, when the giant dies, or when it uses Ice Wolves again.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Ice Armor (requires Frost Rune). When a creature the giant can see rolls an attack against it, the giant gains +6 AC against that attack. After the hit or miss is resolved, the ice breaks. Each creature within 5 ft. of the giant must pass a DC 18 Dexterity save or take 13 (3d8) cold damage.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: Alecto, Megaera, and Tisiphone hunt penitents in Ravenloft. They tempt their target back into wrongdoing before resorting to murder.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: The sisters appear together and may approach in the guise of elderly human women. They lure a penitent with promises of divination and make three attempts to corrupt them again. If all three attempts fail, the sisters try to kill the penitent in public. In combat, use the individual scourges and spellcasting of Alecto, Megaera, and Tisiphone alongside the shared rules below.

gm.title: Fury shared rules
lines:
Printed source. Furies, pp. 79–80. The sisters appear together and speak all humanoid languages. They try three times to divert a target from atonement before trying to kill them in public.
Defenses. Damage reduction 15/good. Immune to paralysis, polymorph, and mind-affecting effects.
Scourge. The +3 scourge works like a whip that deals 1d4 lethal damage before modifiers. A Fury may substitute it for her claw attacks. Use the attack and ability damage listed for that sister. Rake (Ex) is +9 melee for 1d4 + 1 damage.
Alter Self (Sp). At will as a standard action, a Fury can take the form of an elderly human woman indefinitely. Caster level 10.
Breath Weapon (Su, 3/day). Fill one adjacent square with foul air. Apply stinking cloud as cast by an 8th-level sorcerer, with a DC 16 Fortitude save.
Find Penitent (Su). Furies can locate a target who seeks redemption at the invitation or embrace stage of corruption. The target cannot hide from them, even with magic.
Gaseous Death (Su). At 0 HP, a Fury and her scourge dissolve into smoke. Surviving sisters continue to fight, though the last survivor tries to flee. If a sister survives, the slain Furies return at full HP after 24 hours. To kill them permanently, all three must die within the same 24 hours and an Innocent must deal the killing blows. Their scourges remain after permanent death.
Weaknesses. A good cleric or a paladin can turn each Fury separately by invoking her true name. A turning attempt cannot destroy, rebuke, or command her. A Fury cannot deliberately harm a good creature except with her breath weapon.

gm.title: Description
lines: Kostchtchie grants some frost giant devotees immense strength and a bitter chill that drives them to seek out fights.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Chilling Aura. A creature starting its turn within 10 ft. of the fury must pass a DC 20 Constitution save or take 11 (2d10) cold damage.
Magic Resistance. The fury has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Fist or Rock in any combination.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) cold damage. The cold damage rises to 17 (5d6) if Chilling Aura damaged the target since the end of the fury's last turn.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +13 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Charge. Move up to the fury's speed toward an enemy it can see.
